item.title: No. 1 UH basketball vs. Oakland: How to watch, what to know
item.description: UH guard Mercy Miller has averaged 16 points over the previous four games, including a career-high 21 points in the Cougars' victory over Kansas to win the Players Era 8 championship. (Abbie Parr/Associated Press) Top-ranked Houston begins a four-game homestand against Oakland. When: 6:30 p.m. Friday. Where: Fertitta Center (7,035). TV: CBS Sports Network with Tom McCarthy (play-by-play), Chris Walker (analyst) and Gary Parrish (sideline reporter). Radio: 950 AM with Jeremy Branham (play-by-play). The game also will be streamed on The Varsity app, SiriusXM (channels 139 and 237 and the SiriusXM app (channel 961). Houston vs. Oakland Series history: Tied 1-1. Last meeting: No. 1 Houston won 78-45 on Nov. 12, 2025, at Fertitta Center. Oakland Grizzlies Location: Rochester, Mich. Conference: Horizon League Coach: Greg Kampe (732-577 in 43 seasons at Oakland). Record: 1-7 About the Grizzlies: Oakland plays 13 of its first 15 games on the road. The Grizzlies are coming off a 95-49 loss to Purdue. The nonconference schedule includes ranked opponents Michigan, Alabama, Purdue, Houston, Arkansas and Michigan State. ... Oakland led Arizona State by 14 points in the second half before losing 68-65 on Nov. 18. ... Oakland is 3-56 all-time against ranked opponents. Its last win against a ranked opponent came against No. 12 Kentucky, 80-76, in first round of the 2024 NCAA Tournament. ... Chris Fields Jr. had 18 points, 10 rebounds and five steals against Purdue. He has six double-doubles in eight games. ... Nassim Mashhour, who was limited to 10 games last season because of an injury, has a team-high 22 3-pointers. The Grizzlies have made at least one 3-pointer in 1,207 consecutive games dating to 1988, the fourth-longest active streak behind UNLV, Duke and East Tennessee State. ... Oakland has outrebounded five opponents, including Michigan (44-42) and Alabama (37-31). ... Greg Kampe ranks ninth among active Division I coaches with 732 wins. He is seventh all-time in Division I games coached with 1,310. ... The last time the Grizzlies faced the No. 1 team was 2025, when they played back-to-back games against Purdue and Houston. item.title: Luis Díaz could play striker for Bayern Munich in absence of Harry Kane, Ismael Saibari
item.description: Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Bundesliga via Getty Images | Bundesliga via Getty Images Bayern Munich are in the midst of an attacking injury crisis. The misfortune began in October. Luis Díaz suffered a muscle tear in a 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal. One week later, Serge Gnabry and Ismael Saibari sustained first-half injuries in another 2-2 draw — this time against bitter rivals Borussia Dortmund in the Bundesliga. Harry Kane and Michael Olise’s fitness remained the only silver lining in a dark cloud until disaster struck. Kane and Olise left the field in the first half of Bayern’s 1-1 draw against 1. FC Köln. The Englishman was forced off after enduring a left ankle ligament tear, while Olise’s foot injury cut his outing short. Worst-case scenario unlocked. However, there may yet be a glimmer of hope. Díaz is nearing a return to action, though he may not be deployed in his natural role on the left wing. According to CBS Sports Golazo pundit Raphael Honigstein (via @iMiaSanMia ), Bayern could use the Colombian international at striker for the foreseeable future. “Playing Luis Díaz upfront in Harry Kane and Ismael Saibari’s absence is an idea that has been floated, and is the most promising one. He’s done that successfully for Liverpool and can play in that position. At least until Christmas, that’s probably going to be Bayern’s preferred option,” Honigstein said. Bayern are thin at center-forward, making Díaz a logical option. Jamal Musiala is another candidate through the middle, but given his limited experience leading the line, Lucho may be the cleaner fit. Join the conversation! item.title: Kentucky vs. Louisville viewing info, what to watch for, odds, and predictions
item.description: Kentucky Football enters the season finale limping, losing three straight and battling several injuries. However, they face the Louisville Cardinals in the annual Governor’s Cup, who have found their stride and are riding a six-game winning streak. While this game doesn’t have consequences for the College Football Playoff, as many believed just weeks ago, rivalry bragging rights are on the line, and Louisville has won two straight in the series. The Governor’s Cup is always one of the most anticipated games on Kentucky’s schedule, but Saturday’s matchup carries additional significance with Will Stein on the sideline. The first-year Wildcat head coach grew up in a Kentucky family and was a Kentucky fan, but played his college career for Louisville. He, like anyone, understands the importance of this rivalry game, calling it “the game of the season” in his press conference this week. “It’s about an opportunity to go out there at home and finish the season the way we want.” Let’s take a look at the matchup. Limit Explosive Plays Louisville’s offense is one of the best Kentucky will play this season. Led by running back Isaac Brown and wide receiver Tre Richardson, the Cardinals rank 12th nationally in total offense. Additionally: 38.6 points per game (8th nationally); 36.6 points per game against FBS opponents. Offensive EPA Per Play: 10th nationally Rushing Success Rate: 13th nationally Offensive explosiveness: 21st nationally The Cardinals will generate offense, but the Wildcats must limit the explosive plays, something Missouri was able to generate consistently last week. With a rushing-leaning offense centered around Brown, the Wildcats must be able to play physical at the line of scrimmage and get some pressure in the backfield, which they have struggled to do of late. They also need to be wary of the Cardinals attempting to throw it over the top if they are able to establish the running game. Red Zone Efficiency For the first half of the season, Kentucky was one of the SEC’s best at scoring in the red zone. Since the bye week, the Wildcats have severely struggled in the category. That was on full display against Missouri as the Wildcats scored just one touchdown and 14 total points in seven red zone trips. For the Wildcats, two big pieces of their red zone attack are running back CJ Baxter, who has been battling injuries, and tight end Willie Rodriguez, who played his worst game of the season against the Tigers. item.content:encoded: Kentucky Football enters the season finale limping, losing three straight and battling several injuries. However, they face the Louisville Cardinals in the annual Governor’s Cup, who have found their stride and are riding a six-game winning streak. While this game doesn’t have consequences for the College Football Playoff, as many believed just weeks ago, rivalry bragging rights are on the line, and Louisville has won two straight in the series. The first-year Wildcat head coach grew up in a Kentucky family and was a Kentucky fan, but played his college career for Louisville. He, like anyone, understands the importance of this rivalry game, calling it “the game of the season” in his press conference this week. “It’s about an opportunity to go out there at home and finish the season the way we want.” Let’s take a look at the matchup. Limit Explosive Plays Louisville’s offense is one of the best Kentucky will play this season. Led by running back Isaac Brown and wide receiver Tre Richardson, the Cardinals rank 12th nationally in total offense. Additionally: 38.6 points per game (8th nationally); 36.6 points per game against FBS opponents. Offensive EPA Per Play: 10th nationally Rushing Success Rate: 13th nationally Offensive explosiveness: 21st nationally The Cardinals will generate offense, but the Wildcats must limit the explosive plays, something Missouri was able to generate consistently last week. With a rushing-leaning offense centered around Brown, the Wildcats must be able to play physical at the line of scrimmage and get some pressure in the backfield, which they have struggled to do of late. They also need to be wary of the Cardinals attempting to throw it over the top if they are able to establish the running game. Red Zone Efficiency For the first half of the season, Kentucky was one of the SEC’s best at scoring in the red zone. Since the bye week, the Wildcats have severely struggled in the category. That was on full display against Missouri as the Wildcats scored just one touchdown and 14 total points in seven red zone trips. For the Wildcats, two big pieces of their red zone attack are running back CJ Baxter, who has been battling injuries, and tight end Willie Rodriguez, who played his worst game of the season against the Tigers. Facing one of the nation’s best offenses, Kentucky must find ways to finish drives of their own, and that is an area Will Stein is focusing on going into Saturday. With Baxter’s status up in the air for Louisville, Rodriguez will be a priority target, and I would expect to see some creative offensive sets in the red zone. Limit Mistakes The margin of error in college football is small. Turnovers, costly penalties and mistakes in critical moments can easily play yourself out of a game, rather than your opponent defeating you. In his weekly press conference, Stein talked about “going to the doctor” and evaluating the game tape from the Missouri game on Sunday. He and the staff believe that of the 78 plays, 6 of them decided the outcome of the game. “That’s less than 10% of the plays, but that’s how small the margins are. You’re playing in what I’ve described to you guys is as close to the NFL as you can as you can be. If you give teams extra possessions, specifically when you’re driving in the red zone three times and turn the ball over, it’s virtually impossible to overcome.” If the Wildcats want to finish the regular season on a high note, they need to play sound and fundamental football, and not beat themselves. K ey Players RB Isaac Brown, 5-9, 190 lbs 834 rushing yards (35th nationally) on 120 carries 7.0 YPC (9th nationally) 8 TDs WR Tre Richardson, 5-10, 175 lbs 822 receiving yards (37th nationally) 58 receptions (42nd nationally) 5 TDs DL Clev Lubin, 6-3, 260 lbs 9 sacks (11th nationally) 2 forced fumbles Kentucky Wildcats vs. Louisville Cardinals Game Time: 12:00 PM EST on November 28, 2026 Location: Kroger Field in Lexington, Kentucky TV Channel: ESPN2 will have coverage for this game. Announcers: Jay Alter, Tom Luginbill, and Lauren Sisler will be on the call. Online Stream: WatchESPN and the ESPN app. Radio: Tom Leach and Jeff Piecoro have the UK radio call on the UK Sports Network . Satellite Radio: XM Channel 203, Sirius Channel 98, Internet Channel 966 Replay: Watch ESPN and SEC Network (check local listings). Rosters: UK | UofL Stats to Know: UK | UofL Advanced Stats Weather.com Forecast : Lower 50s to upper 40s with a breeze and some clouds. Odds: FanDuel Sportsbook has Louisville listed as a 2.5-point favorite, with a point total of 54.5. ESPN has the Wildcats as an underdog as well, giving them a 35.6% win probability. Predictions: PickWatch , which rounds up predictions across the internet, has Louisville getting 76% of the picks for this one. TeamRankings pick the Cardinals to win 28-26. DRatings also gives Louisville the edge, 27-24. Will Stein understands the importance of this game, and I do believe Kentucky is the better all-around team. For that reason, I am going with a 27-24 victory, Kentucky! Send us your score predictions in the comments section! And Go Cats!!

item.title: What Mason Rudolph was made to do by the Steelers on Thursday after Aaron Rodgers was waived
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images Aaron Rodgers has officially been released by the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback’s reported ultimatum to head coach Mike McCarthy, followed by some controversial accusations on the Pat McAfee Show, forced the Steelers’ hand. Pittsburgh take on the Denver Broncos on Friday, and with Rodgers now gone, Mason Rudolph is being readied to fill his shoes. Mason Rudolph had to do extra work to be ready for Steelers vs Broncos after Aaron Rodgers was cut Rodgers was expected to start for the Pittsburgh Steelers against the Denver Broncos on Friday. The 42-year-old was involved in training this week, with McCarthy even allowing him to take over the play calling upon his request. However, after practice on Tuesday, Rodgers demanded a system change and threatened to leave if he didn’t get his wish. He was then released by the team. Rudolph, who hadn’t been involved in first-team reps all week, was made to do some extra work on Thursday to get him ready for the Black Friday game against the Broncos. That’s according to Jay Glazer, who said on Fox Sports : “They now have Mason Rudolph, who was not able to practice. “Today (Thursday), they had a walkthrough and a little extra work to get Mason Rudolph some work in.” Rudolph has played just four times for the Steelers this season, all on late garbage-time drives. He has averaged 1-4 passing for two yards and four carries for 10 rushing yards in those games. The 31-year-old last started a game for the Steelers in November last year, a 31-28 loss against the Chicago Bears. He completed 24 of 31 passes for 171 yards, one touchdown, and one interception, while adding seven rushing yards on three carries and losing one fumble. It is a tough ask for Rudolph to get up to speed this quickly, but the Steelers will be hoping that the extra work they put in on Thursday will pay off. item.title: Josh Allen matches Russell Wilson with 98 wins in nine seasons
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 26: Josh Allen #17 of the Buffalo Bills scrambles in the first quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Highmark Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images For all the records Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen has broken lately, this might be one that means a little more to him. After all, if you’ve listened to enough of Allen’s postgame press conferences, you know there’s one statistic he cares about more than any other — wins. With Buffalo’s 13-10 win over the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, Allen has now won 98 regular-season games, tying Russell Wilson for the most wins by a starting quarterback in his first nine NFL seasons. Wilson, who entered the league in 2012, never had a losing season during his first nine years with the Seattle Seahawks. He won double-digit games in eight of those nine seasons, including a career-high 13 in 2013. Allen, on the other hand, won just five games as a rookie in 2018. A year later, the Bills were back in the playoffs, and they haven’t had a losing season since. In fact, Buffalo extended its franchise record to eight consecutive winning seasons just last week with a win over the Miami Dolphins. Allen moved past Patrick Mahomes (95) on this particular list two weeks ago when the Bills beat the New York Jets. Now, having picked up another win at Mahomes’ expense, Allen has caught Wilson, too. Allen completed just 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards while adding 43 yards on the ground. The real hero of the night was Tyler Bass who scored seven of the team’s 13 points – including the game winning field goal from 57 yards. But football is a team sport, and Allen’s contribution still counts. And the win is his to claim. The Bills will be in New England next week, where Allen will have his first opportunity to take sole possession of the NFL record. Allen still has six regular-season games left in his ninth season. That gives him some time to make life a little more difficult for the next quarterback chasing this record.

item.title: How to watch Wisconsin’s game vs. Minnesota on Friday
item.description: IOWA CITY, IA - OCTOBER 31: Wisconsin Badgers quarterback Colton Joseph (1) pitches the ball to Wisconsin Badgers running back Darrion Dupree (6) during a Big Ten Conference college football game between the Wisconsin Badgers and the Iowa Hawkeyes on October 31, 2026, at Kinnick Stadium in Iowa City, IA. (Photo by Keith Gillett/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers are hosting the Minnesota Gophers on Friday, looking to avenge their recent losses in the rivalry for the Axe Trophy, as they hope to reach eight wins for the first time under Luke Fickell. Wisconsin has not fared well in this rivalry recently, losing four of the last five games, including two straight by double digits. But the Badgers have enjoyed their best season to date under Luke Fickell, going 7-4 thus far, while Minnesota has experienced some major highs and lows in a 6-5 season. The Badgers have a pair of ranked wins, but their increased win total has been overshadowed by ugly losses to the Iowa Hawkeyes and Maryland Terrapins, once again putting the pressure on Fickell, especially with a new Athletic Director in town. Minnesota, on the other hand, has beaten Iowa and Northwestern, while playing Indiana close. But they were also blown out by Mississippi State, Purdue, UCLA, and Penn State, with three of those losses coming by 25+. The Gophers did secure a key win over Northwestern to get bowl-eligible last week, and they’ll look to play spoiler to the Badgers again on Friday. Here are all the details for Friday’s game between Wisconsin and Minnesota. Date: Friday, November 27th Time: 6:30 p.m. Channel: NBC Stadium: Camp Randall Stadium Spread: Wisconsin -8.5 Total: 37.5 points

item.title: Washington Commanders vs Arizona Cardinals Week 12: Five Questions with Revenge of the Birds
item.description: It’s week 12 of the NFL season and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 3-8 Arizona Cardinals team on the road at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, AZ this coming Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Cardinals are a team in transition; they only had a placeholder QB to start the season in Jacoby Brissett. They traded him away to the Ravens in week 9, backup QB Gardner Minshew sustained a season-ending injury after his first start, and now the Cardinals are deciding between rookie 3rd-round pick Carson Beck (who is injured) and recently-signed 40-year old journeyman Josh Johnson to lead the offense. The Cardinals are in their 4th year of GM Monti Ossenfort (formerly of the Titans) and 1st year of HC Mike LaFleur (formerly of the Rams, and younger brother of Packers’ HC Matt LaFleur). On offense, the Cardinals are coached by HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett, with LaFleur calling the plays. As a McVay disciple, LaFleur runs a McVay/Shanahan style offense that is built on formation shifts, pre-snap motion, and play-action passing to confuse opposing defenses. As part of this tree, the offense is built around an outside-zone run offense with pin-and-pull concepts designed to move defenders with angles and set up play-action and bootlegs. Arizona’s primary weapon in the passing game has been TE Trey McBride, who has 689 receiving yards on 87 receptions so far this year. Given how many receptions Washington seems to give up to TEs, this should be a matchup to watch. Overall, Arizona’s offense ranks 23rd in passing yards/game and 27th in rushing yards/game . Note that 3rd-overall pick in the 2026 draft Jeremiyah Love is still on injured reserve, which no doubt impacts the running game. item.content:encoded: It’s week 12 of the NFL season and the 4-5-1 Washington Commanders will be facing a 3-8 Arizona Cardinals team on the road at State Farm Stadium in Glendale, AZ this coming Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET. The Cardinals are a team in transition; they only had a placeholder QB to start the season in Jacoby Brissett. They traded him away to the Ravens in week 9, backup QB Gardner Minshew sustained a season-ending injury after his first start, and now the Cardinals are deciding between rookie 3rd-round pick Carson Beck (who is injured) and recently-signed 40-year old journeyman Josh Johnson to lead the offense. The Cardinals are in their 4th year of GM Monti Ossenfort (formerly of the Titans) and 1st year of HC Mike LaFleur (formerly of the Rams, and younger brother of Packers’ HC Matt LaFleur). On offense, the Cardinals are coached by HC Mike LaFleur and OC Nathaniel Hackett, with LaFleur calling the plays. As a McVay disciple, LaFleur runs a McVay/Shanahan style offense that is built on formation shifts, pre-snap motion, and play-action passing to confuse opposing defenses. As part of this tree, the offense is built around an outside-zone run offense with pin-and-pull concepts designed to move defenders with angles and set up play-action and bootlegs. Arizona’s primary weapon in the passing game has been TE Trey McBride, who has 689 receiving yards on 87 receptions so far this year. Given how many receptions Washington seems to give up to TEs, this should be a matchup to watch. Overall, Arizona’s offense ranks 23rd in passing yards/game and 27th in rushing yards/game . Note that 3rd-overall pick in the 2026 draft Jeremiyah Love is still on injured reserve, which no doubt impacts the running game. On defense, the Cardinals had been led by DC Nick Rallis, a holdover from Jonathan Gannon’s coaching staff. However, Rallis was fired after giving up 34 points to the Chiefs. Teryl Austin, former DC of the Steelers, will be taking over as defensive playcaller and interim DC. It’s anyone’s guess what Austin’s defense will look like, but he is taking over a defense ranked 19th against the pass and 27th against the run . Despite DE Josh Sweat ranking 13th in the NFL in pass rush win rate , the Cardinals overall have been ranked 13th in pass rush win rate and ranked 22nd in run stop win rate. I asked Seth Cox of Revenge of the Birds five questions about the state of the Cardinals and what to look for in this game. 1) The Cardinals have just fired DC Nick Rallis. What did you think of Rallis, how much of the problems on defense were due to him vs personnel, and what do you think will change with Teryl Austin replacing him? I think Rallis was terrible at his job and should have been fired with all of the Jonathan Gannon staff, but no one wanted this job. He had great ideas, but they are unable to execute them because of their talent, and that makes you bad at your job. If you are continually doing the square peg, round hole thing and continually terrible, that is on you to not make changes and instead put new pieces out there and fail the same way. I think Rallis’ schemes are excellent, but he needs the right personnel to get it to work. 2) What are the early returns on HC Mike LaFleur and what do you think of the Cardinals’ coaching staff in general? Hard to tell. Terrible defense. Terrible quarterback situation. Terrible roster construction from the general manager. So, let’s just say it’s unfair to judge him, but his offensive scheme is awful thus far and that is super disappointing. But is it because the roster is awful? Likely. Could his scheme also be awful? Absolutely. 3) What do you think of GM Monti Ossenfort and how he is building the team? He legitimately may be the worst GM in NFL history if they lose out this season. Seriously, think about all the bad GM’s and we are approaching the point where if Ossenfort loses out, his win percentage as GM would be worse than Matt Millen’s. Things have not been going well in Arizona and Ossenfort is a massive reason why. 4) It’s currently unclear if Carson Beck or Josh Johnson will start at QB this week. What have you seen out of each of them and what will the offense look like with them at the helm? Bad? I mean Josh Johnson had been here 12 days so I guess you can make an exception, but Beck was mostly bad, then has been dealing with a recurring back injury. It makes the entire situation for the Cardinals and their fans even harder to understand and stomach because you can’t even get to enjoy watching Beck play because his back is so bad. So instead, we get 40-year old Josh Johnson and I guess we will see if newly brought back Kedon Slovis will be the young player we get to watch and hope turns into something. This place sucks. 5) How should Washington gameplan for this matchup on both sides of the ball? Show up? Seriously, Teryl Austin will be calling the defense for the first time, but the talent is what it is. So, when you look at what the Cardinals defense has done well, it wasn’t terrible in pass coverage, but mainly that’s because it is so awful at stopping the run that other teams don’t throw the ball much. When you actually want to throw the ball, you’ll see no pass rush, and that “good enough” coverage is really tough to maintain when you are covering for more than 3.5 seconds. On offense, nothing. They don’t run the ball well, they don’t throw the ball well. It’s genuinely miserable to watch. Outside of a miraculous quarter and some time against Dallas, the Arizona Cardinals have five touchdowns scored since the Detroit Lions loss. Five touchdowns in six games and three quarters. Three touchdowns in one quarter against the Cowboys (I know you guys will enjoy that nugget). This offense stinks. Anyways, Commanders win and cover unless Austin is somehow a wizard. Commanders 31 Cardinals 10 Good luck and good health in this one to you all. There will be no companion article to this one, as Seth is enjoying Thanksgiving and probably scouting new GM candidates, so it was generous of him to answer our questions here. Thanks again to Seth Cox for taking time out of his day to answer our questions about the Cardinals.

item.title: Ilia Malinin posts record short program score to lead NHK Trophy
item.description: Ilia Malinin recorded the highest short program score in history at NHK Trophy in Tokyo to take a whopping 18.03-point lead into Saturday's free skate. Malinin, the three-time world champion, tallied 114.81 points with a quadruple flip, triple Axel and a quad Lutz-triple toe loop combination in his "Cantata Memoria — For the Children" skate. He beat the previous record score of 113.87 set by Nathan Chen at the 2022 Olympics. Due to scoring system changes, skaters are able to score higher in short programs in this Olympic cycle than in previous Olympic cycles. FIGURE SKATING: Full Results | Broadcast Schedule Malinin is bidding for a ninth consecutive Grand Prix win dating to 2023 and a fifth consecutive trip to December's Grand Prix Final, the second-most prestigious annual event after March's World Championships. Malinin will qualify for the Final in China if he finishes anywhere on the podium on Saturday. Olympic bronze medalist Shun Sato of Japan is the distant second-place skater going into the free skate after landing a quad Lutz that was one-quarter under-rotated and a quad toe-triple toe combination in his short. Earlier, world bronze medalists Emilea Zingas and Vadym Kolesnik topped the rhythm dance as they seek to sweep their two Grand Prix regular season starts en route to the Grand Prix Final. Fellow Americans Christina Carreira and Anthony Ponomarenko are second -- 2.34 points back -- as they vie with third-pace Finns Juulia Turkkila and Matthias Versluis for the last Grand Prix Final spot. Two-time world medalist Mone Chiba leads after the women's short program, looking to give Japan a sweep of the six Grand Prix regular season women's titles. The only nation to do that in Grand Prix history was Russia in 2019. In pairs, world champions Minerva Hase and Nikita Volodin of Germany are followed by Yuna Nagaoka and Sumitada Morgiuchi of Japan, with both of those teams in line to secure the last two Grand Prix Final spots. Figure skating TV, live stream schedule for 2026-27 season How to watch figure skating’s biggest events, including the Grand Prix Series, on NBC Sports and Peacock. Nick Zaccardi ,

item.title: Do you feel better, worse about Detroit Lions after loss to Bears?
item.description: Nov 26, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift (4) is tripped up by Detroit Lions defensive back Andre Cisco (28) and cornerback Rock Ya-Sin (23) in the first quarter at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It’s never good to lose to a division rival. It’s even harder to swallow the loss when it feels like self-inflicted wounds turned a likely win into painful loss. That’s what Detroit Lions fans are going through this Black Friday, as they try to cope with the Lions blowing a double-digit lead in the fourth quarter to lose a pivotal game to the Chicago Bears. But after the sting of the loss wears off, we’ll have to assess the team and what Thursday’s loss means for the season. Maybe you’re still not over it. Maybe you’re still seething at certain plays or play-calls. But, for now, let’s assess where things are at. Today’s Question of the Day is: Do you feel better, worse, or the same after the Lions’ loss to the Bears? My answer: Thursday’s game confirmed a lot of good things I knew about the Lions. Their run game is back, their offensive line is playing their best football, and this team’s offense will keep them alive in just about any game. Jahmyr Gibbs is an insane weapon to have, and when Jared Goff is dealing, no one can stop them. Remember that going into this game, the Bears were considered one of the best defenses in football. Detroit just hung 549 yards and 35 points on them—and it probably should have been even more. For three straight weeks now, the Lions have played decent-to-great defenses, and they’ve hung at least 30 on each. That has to make you feel pretty good right now. Unfortunately, Thursday also presented the first real test of this defense in months, and they failed spectacularly. All of the problems that we saw earlier in the season—missed assignments, poor run defense, failure to capitalize on opportunities to get off the field—re-emerged. It begs the question as to whether all of Detroit’s defensive improvements over the past couple months were real or the result of playing poor offenses. Particularly concerning is the play of the linebacking corps, where Detroit doesn’t seem to know who they can depend upon. With Jack Campbell out, there is no one linebacker that is the defense’s rock. Derrick Barnes barely played in the first half, Malcolm Rodriguez was a huge liability for most of the day, K.J. Britt’s magic seems to have worn off, and even Trevor Nowaske struggled. Additionally, while Derrick Moore had a fantastic first half, Detroit’s pass rush disappeared in the second. Aidan Hutchinson’s presence was certainly missed constantly in the final two quarters when the Lions defense just needed one more play. The good news is that Detroit’s defense was also missing a few key pieces that they’ll likely get back soon. Defensive end DJ Wonnum and safety Chuck Clark would’ve made a difference in this game. item.title: Seedy K’s GameCap: St. John’s
item.description: The revitalizing University of Louisville Cardinals exclamation-pointed their almost unfathomable first half domination of St. John’s with a tandem of breakaway snowbird deuces. The Cards had jetted to a 12-4 advantage, before eventual leading scorer Seth Trimble had even entered the game off the pine. The lead hovered at around double digits, then rocketed after a Jackson Shelstad triple to unknown parts of the hoops galaxy. With a 57-39 lead at the intermission buzzer, I texted my peeps. “Now I’m really fucking nervous!!!!” I have observed the ever bespoke Don Pitino in such situations in the past. When some team wants to go Barzini or Sollozzo on his squad, he’ll retaliate with extreme prejudice. I viewed the Mardi Gras Massacre over LSU when he was at Kentucky with fascination. Then there was that Pitino-mentored Cardinal turnaround for the ages in the’13 Big East Tourney final. Down 13 to Syracuse at the half, Louisville rampaged the Orange by 30 in the 2d, for a 17 point W. As good and steady and turnover-free mature as the Cards had been to that point, I knew a Johnnie comeback was coming. I doubt I was alone. The Rick is relentless. So it came to pass. Fatigue. Full court pressure. Nerves. An ill-advised strategic maneuver to slow the game with a Prevent Offense, which put a monitor on the Cardinals’ aggressiveness. All that and more, and the lead dwindled and dwindled and dwindled, until St. John’s pulled within a deuce with :13 on the clock, and neither team with a timeout. * * * * * If you’re reading this, you surely know what happened next. The ball was inbounded to Shelstad. Two Johnnies had him trapped along the sideline in the backcourt. It appeared he thought he was hacked, turned his eyes toward ref Tommy Johnson, hoping for a call as he threw the ball off a defender’s leg for a new out of bounds play. Then came that felonious psychedelic refereeing miscue for the ages. The zebra whistled a timeout for Louisville, which they didn’t have, and Shelstad knew they didn’t have, and Shelstad didn’t call. Technical. A pair of Ian Jackson FTs completed the classic Pitino reversal knotting the wacky tilt at 90. Then the Cardiac Cardinals Hall of Fame moment. U of L got the ball inbounds, got it to the frontcourt in Seth Trimble’s hands. He drove but was cut off in the lane, and had the presence of mind to one hand the ball in the direction of Karter Knox and Adrian Wooley along the left sideline. Wooley, with unbelievable calm, snatched the ball, took a sidestep to his left, lifted against two leaping defenders and netted a trey at the buzzer. 93-90. As my guy Smarts said, “Justice was served” for that travesty of a call. * * * * * For any sort of organized appraisal of this beauteous Vegas victory, I’ll have to watch the game in full, maybe next week. item.content:encoded: The revitalizing University of Louisville Cardinals exclamation-pointed their almost unfathomable first half domination of St. John’s with a tandem of breakaway snowbird deuces. The Cards had jetted to a 12-4 advantage, before eventual leading scorer Seth Trimble had even entered the game off the pine. The lead hovered at around double digits, then rocketed after a Jackson Shelstad triple to unknown parts of the hoops galaxy. With a 57-39 lead at the intermission buzzer, I texted my peeps. “Now I’m really fucking nervous!!!!” I have observed the ever bespoke Don Pitino in such situations in the past. When some team wants to go Barzini or Sollozzo on his squad, he’ll retaliate with extreme prejudice. I viewed the Mardi Gras Massacre over LSU when he was at Kentucky with fascination. Then there was that Pitino-mentored Cardinal turnaround for the ages in the’13 Big East Tourney final. Down 13 to Syracuse at the half, Louisville rampaged the Orange by 30 in the 2d, for a 17 point W. As good and steady and turnover-free mature as the Cards had been to that point, I knew a Johnnie comeback was coming. I doubt I was alone. The Rick is relentless. So it came to pass. Fatigue. Full court pressure. Nerves. An ill-advised strategic maneuver to slow the game with a Prevent Offense, which put a monitor on the Cardinals’ aggressiveness. All that and more, and the lead dwindled and dwindled and dwindled, until St. John’s pulled within a deuce with :13 on the clock, and neither team with a timeout. * * * * * If you’re reading this, you surely know what happened next. The ball was inbounded to Shelstad. Two Johnnies had him trapped along the sideline in the backcourt. It appeared he thought he was hacked, turned his eyes toward ref Tommy Johnson, hoping for a call as he threw the ball off a defender’s leg for a new out of bounds play. Then came that felonious psychedelic refereeing miscue for the ages. The zebra whistled a timeout for Louisville, which they didn’t have, and Shelstad knew they didn’t have, and Shelstad didn’t call. Technical. A pair of Ian Jackson FTs completed the classic Pitino reversal knotting the wacky tilt at 90. Then the Cardiac Cardinals Hall of Fame moment. U of L got the ball inbounds, got it to the frontcourt in Seth Trimble’s hands. He drove but was cut off in the lane, and had the presence of mind to one hand the ball in the direction of Karter Knox and Adrian Wooley along the left sideline. Wooley, with unbelievable calm, snatched the ball, took a sidestep to his left, lifted against two leaping defenders and netted a trey at the buzzer. 93-90. As my guy Smarts said, “Justice was served” for that travesty of a call. * * * * * For any sort of organized appraisal of this beauteous Vegas victory, I’ll have to watch the game in full, maybe next week. Some random thoughts. Adrian Wooley not only finished the game, he started it. Scored 8 of U of L’s first 14, when the Cards were up ten at the initial media timeout. Seth Trimble scored on drives to the hoop three straight trips after entering. The likely to be overlooked blessing that was St. J star Tounde Yessoufou committing his third foul at 6:48 of the 1st. And his fourth at 14:18 of the 2d. A floor scramble for the ball which LJ Wells won, getting the ball to Wooley for a 3, and soon to be vanished 68-44 lead. What a steady presence Alvaro Folgueiras was all game. He kept the offense flowing. At least until the Cards went slowdown. Eight rebounds. Again, U of L was solid at the stripe. 19/25. 75%. My ever enduring appreciation of Jefferson Circuit Judge Brian Edwards. Currently eligible Seth Trimble was Player of Game. 33 points. 4 rebounds. 5 assists. That scoring included another shot clock FG, this time a deuce. * * * * * Though my sleep-deprived heart is full at the wondrous second-night-in-a-row win, there I must mention. Pat Kelsey fell into a trap. (He’s not the first.) Louisville should have kept the peddle to the metal. I understand, with the injuries and resulting short bench, fatigue is a major factor. But still, it played right into Pitino’s hand. Cards’ offense turned stagnant. We must remember Obinna Ekezie is young. Patience is required. Karter Knox is obviously going to be a major factor, now that he’s emerging from his coccoon. Silly fouls (in quick succession) are not a good thing. * * * * * Before this Players Era surge against a couple elite foes, based on that what is now ancient history Memphis State meltdown and underperformance against Stetson, the analytics gurus were not kind to the Cardinals. Beating strong teams cures that. U of L has moved up 14 spots at Ken Pomeroy, from #45 to #31. Up 14 spots at Even Miya, from #33 to #19. Up 4 spots at Bart Torvik, from #22 to #18. Tonight, an opportunity for further advancement against consensus Top 15 Tennessee. Because the increasingly irrepressible Louisville Cardinals have bested a pair of top tier opponents in Vegas. That final again: Pat Kelsey’s Louisville 93, Rick Pitino’s St. John’s 90. — c d kaplan

item.title: Australia set to drop Lyon for first New Zealand Test
item.description: Nathan Lyon played twice in Australia's recent 2-1 series defeat in South Africa [Getty Images] Australia are set to drop off-spinner Nathan Lyon for the first Test against New Zealand, with uncapped Corey Rocchiccioli expected to be named in the squad. The omission of Lyon for the Test in Perth from 9-13 December is not thought to be linked to the sandpaper controversy. Lyon was part of the Australia XI in Cape Town in 2018 and, three years later, joined his fellow bowlers in releasing a statement denying involvement in the cheating plot. Lyon has not spoken publicly since the debate over the sandpaper saga reemerged with the allegation raised in former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering The decision to omit Lyon, a mainstay of their team for 15 years, is a significant move by Australia and leaves the 39-year-old's international career at a crossroads. With 577 Test wickets, Lyon is sixth on the all-time list, with more wickets than any Australian apart from the legendary Shane Warne. In terms of off-spinners, only Sri Lankan great Muttiah Muralitharan has more. But Lyon has struggled with form and fitness ever since hobbling out of the second Ashes Test at Lord's in 2023 with a calf injury. In the most recent Ashes series of 2025-26, Lyon did not bowl a ball in the first Test in Perth, was left out of the day-night Test in Brisbane, then suffered a series-ending injury in the third Test in Adelaide. Whereas the omission of Lyon would once have been unthinkable, Australia have recently left him out of their XI on a regular basis in order play an extra seamer. Lyon has repeatedly stated his desire to extend his career in order to win Test series away in India and England - challenges Australia face in 2027. Lyon may still be required on the spin-friendly pitches of India, but 29-year-old Rocchiciolli now has the opportunity to be become Australia's number one. Also an off-spinner, Rocchiciolli offers Australia the option of batting depth - he made 140 for Western Australia against Tasmania in the Sheffield Shield earlier this week. Australia host New Zealand for four Tests in December and January. Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew England outclass Aussies again to take series lead Get cricket news sent straight to your phone

item.title: Bruins' Black Friday Game Carries More Importance Than An Ordinary November Contest
item.description: Bruins' Black Friday Game Carries More Importance Than An Ordinary November Contest originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Bruins won't have much time to recover from their Thanksgiving Eve disappointment. After suffering a 4-2 loss to the Winnipeg Jets on Wednesday, Boston returns to TD Garden on Friday afternoon for a game against the Toronto Maple Leafs. There are certainly worse ways for New England sports fans to spend Black Friday. The timing of the contest makes it particularly interesting for Marco Sturm's team. Boston has enjoyed an encouraging opening portion of the season, but maintaining consistency against Atlantic Division opponents will become increasingly important as the schedule progresses. Toronto Provides A Valuable Measuring Stick There is rarely anything ordinary about a Bruins-Maple Leafs game. The organizations have developed one of hockey's most recognizable rivalries, producing several memorable postseason encounters over the years. item.title: Bayern Munich rule out Joshua Kimmich sanctions after outspoken Jamal Musiala criticism
item.description: Atletico de Madrid v FC Bayern München - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 - Getty Images Sport Bayern Munich have officially confirmed that Joshua Kimmich will not face disciplinary action following his recent public criticism of the club's hierarchy. The German international had spoken out regarding the management's handling of Jamal Musiala, sparking rumors of a potential rift behind the scenes at the Allianz Arena. No fine for outspoken Kimmich Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund has moved to de-escalate tensions within the club by confirming that Kimmich will not be sanctioned for his recent comments . The versatile midfielder had made headlines by publicly questioning the club's leadership following their perceived lack of protection for young star Musiala. Despite the potential for internal friction, the club has decided against imposing a financial penalty on the 31-year-old. Freund addressed the situation during a media briefing, stating that Kimmich will receive "no fine" for his remarks, according to Sky Germany . "We never discussed that, and imposing a fine was never a topic of conversation. We've got intense, important weeks ahead. We need all our energy for that. It's a challenging time, but good things can also come from these times. We'll come through this spell. That's what we're focused on. We're concentrating on the next games - we've got a lot in a short space of time," Freund stated The head coach prioritizes Hamburg clash While the boardroom navigates the fallout from Kimmich’s interview, head coach Vincent Kompany is determined to insulate his squad from the surrounding noise. Ahead of a critical Bundesliga encounter against Hamburg, the Belgian manager insisted that the Musiala debate is not a topic of conversation within his team. He is demanding a professional response following a disappointing 1-2 defeat to Lille in the Champions League. Kompany was blunt when asked about the distractions, stating: "I have to disappoint you, that doesn't occupy everyone. There is a total priority: that is Bayern against HSV, that's all that counts." Kompany coy on Musiala starting spot Regarding the availability of Musiala himself, Kompany remained non-committal about whether the playmaker would return to the starting lineup immediately. Both Musiala and Luis Diaz are nearing full fitness, but the coaching staff is wary of rushing them back given the lack of depth elsewhere in the team. Kompany highlighted that the "entire squad" would be necessary to navigate the high workload of the coming weeks. The manager is expecting his players to show grit in Hamburg to erase the memory of their European setback. "We just have to see that the team fights, is ready to win this game too. That costs a lot of strength and energy now. And my role as coach is that we get points. This game is totally important for us," he concluded. item.title: Legend Chael Sonnen addresses why UFC might not approve Conor McGregor’s return
item.description: Legend Chael Sonnen addresses why UFC might not approve Conor McGregor’s return appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Currently sidelined with an ACL injury and having undergone surgery, Conor McGregor is not expected to return before next year . McGregor came back earlier this year against Max Holloway at UFC 329, but immediately injured his ACL. McGregor, at 38 and with a series of recent losses, wants to come back and have his last UFC fight against Max Holloway. However, the sport’s legend Chael Sonnen addressed why the promotion might not let that happen. “There is nothing historically that would support the idea that Conor is going to return, and I do mean nothing. A guy on his last fight, coming off losses, coming off injuries, not willing to get down to his weight class, not in contendership. There is nothing remotely like that, that takes place in a main event of a UFC. But would you like it to?” Sonnen said on his YouTube channel. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Sonnen also opened up about some of the barriers involved in McGregor’s return. “I do believe Conor wants to fight again. I believe he’s willing to fight again. The sign off here in the issue would simply be the Ultimate Fighting Championship. It’s a triangle. You got the red corner, the blue corner, and the promoter, and they all got to sign off on it. Is the UFC going to sign off on that? “The only thing, the only thing that lends towards a possibility that they will is that Conor has made it clear that he wants to fight Max, and Max has not been booked and/or even discussed to be booked. So if they are reserving Max, it would lend towards a possibility that they’re reserving him for Conor. Things against it. It would be Conor’s final fight. They generally don’t want you to fight out your contract,” Sonnen finished. As of now, neither McGregor nor the UFC have officially opened up about his final fight. item.title: Much-changed Scotland picked to face Argentina
item.description: Rory Darge and Finn Russell are both back for Scotland [SNS] Scotland head coach Gregor Townsend has made 11 changes to his starting XV for Sunday's Nations Championship closer against Argentina at Twickenham (13:10 GMT). Only record try-scoring wing Darcy Graham, centre Rory Hutchinson, scrum-half Jamie Dobie and lock Jonny Gray retain their places, with Finn Russell back at fly-half and flanker Rory Darge returning and captaining the side. Blair Kinghorn, Kyle Steyn, Huw Jones and Darcy Graham return to the back line. Rory Sutherland, Ewan Ashman and D'arcy Rae make up a new front row, Gregor Brown joins Gray in the second row and Josh Bayliss and Magnus Bradbury complete the back row with Darge. The Scots and the Pumas are competing to finish seventh in the tournament. Townsend's Scotland have won four and lost twice so far, while Felipe Contepomi's Argentina have won twice and lost on four occasions. Line-ups Scotland: Blair Kinghorn, Kyle Steyn, Huw Jones, Rory Hutchinson, Darcy Graham, Finn Russell, Jamie Dobie; Rory Sutherland, Ewan Ashman, D'arcy Rae, Gregor Brown, Jonny Gray, Josh Bayliss, Rory Darge (capt), Magnus Bradbury. Replacements: Seb Stephen, Nathan McBeth, Zander Fagerson, Max Williamson, Liam McConnell, Ollie Leatherbarrow, George Horne, Tom Jordan. Argentina: Geronimo Prisciantelli, Rodrigo Isgro, Lucio Cinti, Faustino Sanchez Valarolo, Ignacio Mendy, Tomas Albornoz, Gonzalo Garcia; Rodrigo Martinez, Julian Montoya (capt), Francisco Moreno, Guido Petti, Pedro Rubiolo, Juan Martin Gonzalez, Joaquin Moro, Juan Martin Scelzo. Replacements: Facundo Bosch, Joel Sclavi, Tomas Rapetti, Efrain Elias, Santiago Grondona, Agustin Moyano, Justo Piccardo, Tobias Wade.

item.title: New MI captain: Rohit Sharma appointed as Mumbai Indians skipper replacing Hardik Pandya ahead of IPL 2027
item.description: New MI captain: Rohit Sharma appointed as Mumbai Indians skipper replacing Hardik Pandya ahead of IPL 2027 originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians are reportedly set to name Rohit Sharma captain for IPL 2027, with an announcement expected between November 16 and 18. Earlier, Hardik Pandya was traded to Punjab Kings for Arshdeep Singh. Hardik won 15 of 39 matches as MI captain, and the team finished ninth in IPL 2026. Rohit Sharma returns as MI captain, replacing Hardik Pandya ahead of IPL 2027 Mumbai Indians have announced that they have handed their captaincy back to Rohit Sharma, almost three years after Hardik Pandya replaced him ahead of the 2024 season. The move has ended one of the most controversial leadership changes in IPL history. On November 27 at 5:45 p.m. IST, MI officially announced Rohit's return to captaincy via their social media accounts.. Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo https://t.co/YUqYZTQxu9 — Mumbai Indians (@mipaltan) November 27, 2026 MORE: MI retention list for IPL 2027: Retained and released players Hardik Pandya's three years as Mumbai Indians captain Hardik returned to Mumbai Indians from Gujarat Titans in November 2023 and was immediately named captain, replacing Rohit Sharma, who had led the franchise to five titles. He arrived with a strong record, having captained Gujarat to the 2022 title. The move still divided fans, and the home crowd at the Wankhede Stadium booed him through the 2024 season. That season went badly. Mumbai finished last, with four wins and ten defeats for eight points and a net run rate of minus 0.318, in what was reported as the franchise's worst IPL campaign. The 2025 season was better. MI finished fourth in the league stage and beat Gujarat Titans in the Eliminator before losing Qualifier 2 to the Punjab Kings. Suryakumar Yadav scored 717 runs, and Trent Boult took 22 wickets, and it looked as if the team had steadied under Hardik. That recovery did not last. In 2026, Mumbai again won only four of their 14 games and finished ninth, the second time in three years they ended in the bottom two. Ryan Rickelton scored 448 runs, and Allah Ghazanfar took 15 wickets, but there was little else to celebrate. Batting coach Kieron Pollard admitted late in the season that Hardik's stint "has not gone as well" as the player or the franchise had hoped, and reports said the management was not keen to keep him as captain. MORE: MI squad 2027 team list: Full players list of Mumbai Indians Season League finish Outcome 2024 10th 4 wins, 10 defeats; failed to qualify 2025 4th Won Eliminator, lost Qualifier 2 2026 9th 4 wins, 10 defeats; failed to qualify Across his tenure, Hardik recorded 15 wins and 24 defeats in 39 matches as captain, according to figures cited by ANI. Mumbai also missed the playoffs in two of those three seasons despite having a squad rated among the strongest in the tournament. Former India batter Ambati Rayudu has said Hardik should play purely as a player for at least one season, whether he stays at Mumbai or moves, and focus on his game rather than leadership. MORE: How Rohit Sharma and Virat Kohli reacted to MS Dhoni's IPL and cricket retirement Rohit Sharma's return makes sense, but Mumbai Indians must plan beyond it The case for the change is easy to make. Rohit is the most successful captain in MI's history, with five titles in 2013, 2015, 2017, 2019 and 2020, and the team has not looked like contenders in two of the last three seasons. Adding Arshdeep to a bowling attack led by Jasprit Bumrah would also provide a returning captain with a better pace unit than MI has had. There is also a fair argument on the other side. Rohit turns 40 on April 30, during the 2027 season, and he no longer plays T20Is or Tests for India. A captain at that stage is a short-term answer, not a long-term plan. The sensible view is that this decision is the right move for 2027 and that the real test for the Mumbai Indians is whether they use the year to prepare the next captain rather than waiting for another reset. item.title: Rohit Sharma back as MI captain for IPL 2027: Inside story of how Mumbai Indians convinced 'Hitman' to take over from Hardik Pandya
item.description: Rohit Sharma back as MI captain for IPL 2027: Inside story of how Mumbai Indians convinced 'Hitman' to take over from Hardik Pandya originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Mumbai Indians have officially named Rohit Sharma captain for IPL 2027. Rohit first suggested Tilak Varma, but the franchise asked him to lead again. Kieron Pollard’s new support staff includes Uthappa, McClenaghan, Dilip and Kulkarni, all reportedly close to Rohit. MI captain for IPL 2027: Rohit Sharma officially takes over captaincy from Hardik Pandya Rohit Sharma is the Mumbai Indians captain again. The franchise confirmed the appointment on Friday evening, ending three seasons under Hardik Pandya and handing the job back to the man who won them all five of their titles. Mumbai announced it on their social channels with the line “Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo”, at 5:45 p.m. IST in a nod to the number 45 Rohit wore through his years at the club. Smile, everybody smile 💙 #MumbaiIndians #CaptainRo pic.twitter.com/YUqYZTQxu9 — Mumbai Indians (@mipaltan) November 27, 2026 The Indian Express had reported earlier in the month that the five-time champions were likely to make the change, and that Rohit had agreed to it after the franchise approached him. The decision did not come as a surprise, particularly because Mumbai have carried out a complete overhaul of their support staff over the past fortnight. A change at the top of the dressing room was widely expected to follow, and the franchise has settled on the most familiar name available to it. It is understood that Mumbai wanted Rohit to take over from Pandya midway through the last IPL, at a time when the team was in dire straits. The change is now formal, with the mini-auction in Goa on December 16. Why Mumbai Indians decided to replace Hardik Pandya as captain The results under Pandya’s leadership gave the franchise little reason to wait. Mumbai lost 10 of their 14 games last season, finished ninth in the table and stretched their wait for a title to six years, which is a long drought by their own standards. Across the three seasons he led them, Pandya captained Mumbai in 39 matches and won 15 of them. Rohit’s own record in the job reads 87 wins from 158 matches, with five titles and five wins from five finals, three of those against Chennai Super Kings. According to Express, Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah have been part of the setup for a long time, so a fresh face was certainly possible. Tilak Varma, who is regarded as a future leader, was a natural choice as well if the team wanted to look ahead of 2027. The franchise instead went back to Rohit, as they allegedly believe that the 39-year-old is the best person to lead in the next edition, with a mega auction soon to follow in 2028. The franchise instead went back to Rohit, as they allegedly believe that the 39-year-old is the best person to lead in the next edition, with a mega auction soon to follow in 2028. How Mumbai Indians convinced Rohit Sharma to take the captaincy again Rohit, it seems, did not push for the job himself, and he first named Tilak as the person who should lead the side. “Rohit initially had suggested Tilak Varma’s name but the franchise has requested him to take over captaincy which he has now agreed,” the source told Express. The source also described the extent to which the former captain was involved in the planning. “There were a series of talks that had happened before he flew to New Zealand and Rohit’s suggestions were sought during appointment of new coaches as well,” he added. Tilak is expected to be named his deputy, although Mumbai have not confirmed the vice-captaincy alongside the captaincy announcement. Hardik Pandya has left Mumbai Indians for Punjab Kings in the Arshdeep Singh trade The question of what Pandya would do under a new captain has already been settled. He has been traded to Punjab Kings in a straight swap for Arshdeep Singh, with both players valued at INR 18 crore and nobody else involved in the deal. RevSportz reported that Mumbai held talks with Pandya in June, August and September, and that four options were on the table. Kolkata Knight Riders offered Cameron Green and a fast bowler, Rajasthan Royals offered Yashasvi Jaiswal, Punjab offered Arshdeep, and the fourth was for Pandya to stay one more season before the mega auction. The franchise attracted heavy criticism when it appointed Pandya as captain after an all-cash trade from Gujarat Titans before the 2024 season, and the crowd at the Wankhede Stadium booed him repeatedly during home games. His exit removes the awkwardness of a replaced captain sharing a dressing room with his successor. Why Rohit Sharma is the right captain for Mumbai Indians in IPL 2027 The decision to turn back to Rohit Sharma looks sensible, because it matches both the team’s recent results and the changes made behind the scenes. A ninth-place finish and 10 defeats in 14 games left the franchise with little room to continue as before, and the dressing room needed a leader who commands instant respect. Rohit’s record speaks for itself, and the fact that he had to be persuaded rather than the other way around is a pleasing detail. His early suggestion of Tilak Varma shows that he is thinking about the team’s future, and a season or two under his guidance could be the ideal preparation phase for the youngster. The reunion with Kieron Pollard and the arrival of Robin Uthappa, Mitchell McClenaghan, T Dilip and Dhawal Kulkarni also give the setup a familiar flavour, which could help the squad settle quickly after a disappointing campaign. The challenge now is the squad rather than the dressing room. Mumbai go to the auction with nine places to fill, Arshdeep Singh replacing Pandya as the headline name, and a side that has not reached a final since 2020. Mumbai will still need results to back up the story, but the plan makes sense. Here is how the captaincy changed hands and what pushed it back in his direction. 2013: Rohit Sharma replaces Ricky Ponting and wins Mumbai Indians their first IPL title Rohit was handed the captaincy midway through the 2013 season after Ricky Ponting, who had won three and lost three of his six matches in charge, dropped himself from the side and gave up the role. Kieron Pollard's 60 not out off 32 balls won him the player of the match award. MORE: New MI coach calls themselves 'underdogs' ahead of IPL 2027 season 2015 to 2020: Four more IPL trophies make Rohit Sharma the most successful captain Rohit added titles in 2015, 2017, 2019, and 2020, two of them by a single run. MI beat CSK by 41 runs in the 2015 final, edged Rising Pune Supergiant by one run in 2017, beat CSK by one run in 2019, and saw off Delhi Capitals by five wickets in Dubai in 2020. Those five trophies are the most by any IPL captain. By the end of the 2020 campaign, MI had become the first side to win back-to-back titles in nine years, and Rohit's standing at the franchise looked permanent. IPL 2021 to 2023: Rohit Sharma's returns dry up and the Mumbai Indians slip The run of trophies stopped abruptly. MI finished fifth in 2021 and missed the playoffs on net run rate, then came last in 2022 with four wins from 14 matches after losing their first eight games of the season. Rohit's own form fell away at the same time. He made 381 runs at 29.30 in 2021, 268 runs at 19.14 in 2022 and 332 runs at 20.75 in 2023, with a single fifty across the first two of those seasons. They recovered to finish fourth in 2025 and reach the playoffs, which suggested the arrangement was settling down. The 2026 season undid that. MI won four of 14 and finished ninth, where the second side was eliminated, and suffered their heaviest IPL defeat by runs when CSK beat them by 103. Pandya missed games through unavailability, with Suryakumar Yadav and Jasprit Bumrah standing in. Reports of a breakdown between Pandya and the senior players ran through the campaign. Rohit, restricted to nine matches, made 283 runs at 35.38 with a strike rate of 157.22, having passed 400 in each of the previous two seasons. Kolkata Knight Riders offered Cameron Green and a fast bowler, Rajasthan Royals offered Yashasvi Jaiswal, Punjab offered Arshdeep, and the fourth option was for Pandya to stay one more season before the mega-auction. With Punjab's offer accepted, the captaincy slot became vacant. And now, after a few weeks, MI appointed Sharma as their skipper again. item.title: NFL playoff picture: What does the Bills’ win over the Chiefs mean for AFC standings?
item.description: (Photo by Ryan Kang/Getty Images) | Getty Images Update: Buffalo’s dramatic win over Kansas City on Thanksgiving night kept the Bills atop the AFC standings, and Buffalo is now two games ahead of No. 2 seed Denver for the moment. Kansas City remains in the No. 5 spot, and the Chiefs are one game behind the Broncos in the loss column for the moment. Two AFC titans renew their rivalry on Thanksgiving night, when Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. With both teams near the top of the AFC standings, this game has serious playoff implications for both teams and the AFC as a whole. Let’s dive into the playoff scenarios for both the Bills and the Chiefs ahead of this game. AFC playoff standings Here is the AFC standings ahead of Week 12: 1. Buffalo Bills (9-1) 2. Denver Broncos (8-2) 3. Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 4. Cincinnati Bengals (7-3) 5. Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 6. Cleveland Browns (6-4) 7. Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) 8. New England Patriots (5-5) 9. Houston Texans (4-6) 10. Las Vegas Raiders (4-7) 11. Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 12. New York Jets (3-8) 13. Indianapolis Colts (3-8) 14. Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 15. Miami Dolphins (1-9) 16. Tennessee Titans (1-9) Buffalo Bills playoff picture With a 9-1 record, the Bills sit atop the AFC standings and in position for the No. 1 seed in the conference, as well as the lone bye week. Buffalo also has a comfortable four-game lead over the New England Patriots in the AFC East, but New England won their meeting earlier this season. Should Buffalo win on Thursday night, the Bills would improve to 10-1 and maintain control of the top spot in the conference. A loss, however, would drop Buffalo down to the No. 2 line, and put Kansas City in control of the top seed, at least for the moment. Kansas City Chiefs playoff picture If the NFL playoffs began today, the Kansas City Chiefs would be in, but as the No. 5 seed in the AFC. Why? That comes down to tiebreakers. The Chiefs are tied with the Denver Broncos with an 8-2 record, and those two teams have already split their season series. Since both teams are 3-1 in AFC West games, under the league’s tiebreaking procedures, the next step is win-loss-tied percentage in common games. Both teams have defeated the Las Vegas Raiders, while the Chiefs lost to the Seattle Seahawks, a team the Broncos beat. So for the moment, the Broncos are ahead in the AFC West, and they take the No. 2 spot. However, the Chiefs would not only take control of the top spot in the division, but they would move to the top spot in the AFC overall with a win on Thursday night. That would pull Kansas City level with Buffalo, and the Chiefs would have a head-to-head tiebreaker advantage over the Bills with the victory. With a loss, the Chiefs would remain in the No. 5 spot. They would not be in danger of sliding down further, as both the Cleveland Browns and the Pittsburgh Steelers — the teams at No. 6 and No. 7 right now — are 6-4. But the Chiefs would be

item.title: Celtics Face Fascinating Three-Day Stretch That Could Reveal Plenty About Their Progress
item.description: Celtics Face Fascinating Three-Day Stretch That Could Reveal Plenty About Their Progress originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Boston Celtics return from their Thanksgiving break Friday evening with an interesting stretch of basketball awaiting them. Boston will host the Atlanta Hawks before traveling to San Antonio for a Sunday afternoon game against the Spurs. The two contests provide head coach Joe Mazzulla with opportunities to evaluate his team against considerably different opponents. Boston entered the holiday following Tuesday's 131-116 victory over the Washington Wizards. While that result provided some much-needed momentum, the upcoming weekend could offer a more meaningful indication of where the Celtics stand as November concludes. Atlanta Offers Boston An Opportunity To Establish Consistency The Celtics' first assignment involves taking advantage of a home game against Atlanta. Boston has experienced some inconsistent performances during the opening portion of the season, making Friday an important opportunity to establish a more dependable foundation. Superstar 🌟 https://t.co/nyv08X3W4q — Boston Celtics (@celtics) November 25, 2026 One of the most important objectives involves maintaining offensive organization throughout four quarters. The Celtics possess enough individual talent to create significant scoring runs, but consistently generating quality opportunities becomes particularly valuable against opponents capable of responding with runs of their own. Friday's NBA Cup game also introduces additional competitive significance. The Celtics have an opportunity to finish their group-stage responsibilities while building momentum before another challenging road stretch. MORE : Celtics’ Remaining 2026 Schedule Has Two Very Different Tests Ahead San Antonio Presents A Different Type Of Challenge Sunday's game against the Spurs offers another opportunity to evaluate Boston's offensive execution. Victor Wembanyama's extraordinary size and defensive capabilities present challenges that few NBA teams can replicate. The Celtics will need to make intelligent decisions when attacking the basket while maintaining enough perimeter movement to prevent San Antonio from becoming comfortable defensively. Boston's ability to create opportunities without relying exclusively on difficult individual scoring possessions could become particularly important. There is also a practical challenge associated with traveling following Friday night's home game. The Celtics will have limited preparation time before Sunday's afternoon contest, making their ability to adjust particularly interesting. item.title: McInnes tempers 'anxiety' as Rangers seek top spot
item.description: Ryan Naderi has netted some crucial goals for Derek McInnes this term [SNS] Derek McInnes says Rangers should not experience any anxiety about the prospect of going top of the Scottish Premiership as the Ibrox side look to extend their four-match winning run. Rangers host in-form Falkirk on Saturday (15:00 GMT), who have won six on the bounce in the league, and victory would move McInnes' team top before leaders Celtic travel to face Hearts on Sunday. "I don't think there should be anxiety when you're trying to go top of the league at all," McInnes said. "Obviously, you want to be top of the league come the end of the season. "If you've got an opportunity to go there, it's important you try and take it." Ryan Naderi netted an early second-half equaliser then set up Djeidi Gassama as Rangers turned a 1-0 deficit into a 3-1 lead before Aberdeen scored a consolation in Tuesday's Premiership match at Ibrox. It was Naderi's 11th goal of the season and McInnes spoke of his awareness of the now Czech Republic international last season while managing Hearts, who have used a data analytics firm for much of their recent recruitment. "Last January, obviously, when we first saw that Rangers were linked with Naderi, like everything else, I would say to [Hearts sporting director] Graeme Jones, 'how do they rate him?' "Because you're always curious, it's just the way it is. It's brilliant when you see other teams round about you signing a player that's not rated! "He was someone that I think was well known to them. Brugge had an interest in Ryan, I think, and I think USG potentially had an interest in him as well but the kind of money, the fee, it just went away from them. "The feeling was that he could help Rangers and make them better. "I had a good conversation with Ryan when I first came in the door and what we felt this season could look like for him. "He's stood up brilliantly to the injuries to Youssef [Chermiti] and Lawrence [Shankland] and he's had to be the guy. He's led the line brilliantly and I love the goals he scores. All top strikers have intelligence to be in the right place at the right time." Rangers 'dug it out' despite naivety & complacency - McInnes Visit our Rangers page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views And the manager reiterated his stance about keeping hold of assets like Naderi through January. "These conversations that I have with Jim [Gillespie, chief executive] on a regular basis about players that we should be speaking to and trying to address and secure and give them a wee bit more security and a wee bit more comfort for us, these conversations, I think, have been ongoing," McInnes said. "The club's well aware of what needs to be done and what we shouldn't be doing and Ryan's been part of that conversation." McInnes' side won 2-1 away to Falkirk in September but the Bairns held Danny Rohl's Rangers to a 0-0 draw at Ibrox last season. item.title: Ducks’ Dylan Raiola issues warning about Washington’s motives ahead of Saturday’s rivalry game
item.description: In October, the Oregon Ducks started former walk-on Brock Thomas over Dylan Raiola against the Nebraska Cornhuskers, the program Raiola left after two seasons as its starter. On Wednesday at the Hatfield-Dowlin Complex, Raiola met reporters as Oregon’s starting quarterback heading into his first game against the Washington Huskies, with the Ducks riding a four-game winning streak. Raiola entered that Oct. 17 game at the start of the fourth quarter with Oregon down 14-6 and threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Jamari Johnson with 28 seconds left for a 17-14 win. June 2, 2022; Tempe, Arizona; USA; Chandler quarterback Dylan Raiola throws during a 7-on-7 tournament, an ASU High School Football Showcase. High School Football Asu High School Football Showcase No. 24 Washington comes to Autzen Stadium on Saturday night at 7-4 overall and 4-4 in the Big Ten. The No. 12 Ducks are 8-3 and 6-2, and a win keeps their Big Ten title game hopes alive. “I promise you Washington wants nothing more to come in here and throw a dent in what we got going on. So, we gotta come with it. I know my guys will, and honestly, they’ll probably throw some punches, too. So, we gotta be ready for a heavyweight fight,” Raiola told reporters . He said the Huskies had been sending the “no love lost” message all week, and that Oregon acknowledged it early before turning to preparation. He also said Oregon still regards Washington as a strong team despite the rivalry, and he expects the noise to fall away once the ball is kicked off. “All the emotion, all the hate, everything’s just like ‘All right, it’s football now,'” Raiola said , according to Oregon Ducks On SI’s Chris Wuensch. Raiola says the Ducks have to be ready for a “heavyweight fight” Saturday night. https://t.co/DebKoCPnaa https://t.co/A8f8lznH3u — Bri Amaranthus (@BriAmaranthus) November 26, 2026 Ball security has followed Raiola since October Raiola’s first start for Oregon came on Oct. 10 against the UCLA Bruins, with Dante Moore sidelined by the concussion he suffered at USC, making Raiola the first backup to start at quarterback for Oregon since Braxton Burmeister in 2017. The Ducks turned the ball over seven times in a 17-15 loss. Raiola lost two fumbles in the first half, went 6 of 18 for 43 yards with two interceptions and was replaced by Thomas in the fourth quarter, and Thomas got the start against Nebraska the following week. item.title: Big 12 Conference Championship Game: How Texas Tech clinched a berth
item.description: (Photo by Jocelyn Rafidi/Baylor Athletics/University Images via Getty Images) Update: With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, Texas. Tech clinched a spot in the Big 12 Championship Game against Utah. Rivalry Week is upon us. While some teams are already looking ahead to the College Football Playoff, others are hoping to play spoiler during Rivalry Week. But that proposition has taken on greater importance this year, with the impending move to a 24-team playoff next season. That means these are the last round of Conference Championship Games, so denying a rival a spot in the title game might mean even more this year. In the Big 12, unbeaten Utah has already clinched a spot in the title game. But who will the Utes face: No. 11 Texas Tech, or No. 10 BYU? How Texas Tech can clinch a spot The Red Raiders have the inside track to a spot in the Big 12 title game, and a date with Utah. With a win over TCU on Thanksgiving night, then Texas Tech will clinch the second spot in the Big 12 Championship Game. However, the Red Raiders can still get in if they lose to TCU, provided BYU loses to Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon. How BYU can clinch a spot BYU hosts Cincinnati on Saturday afternoon, but the Cougars might already be eliminated before kickoff. To advance to the Big 12 title game, BYU needs Texas Tech to lose to TCU on Thursday night, and then a win over Cincinnati on Saturday.

item.title: Florida State loses only 2027 running back commit as Jayden Miles flips to Missouri
item.description: The Florida State Seminoles played last Saturday’s 28-10 loss to the NC State Wolfpack with former walk-on Zay Parks taking every running back snap. On Thanksgiving, their 2027 recruiting class lost its only running back commitment as well. Four-star back Jayden Miles of Baton Rouge (La.) Catholic flipped his pledge from Florida State to the Missouri Tigers, Kolby Crawford reported for 247Sports on Thursday. The 6-foot-2, 203-pound Miles had been committed to the Seminoles since June, when he picked them over the Ohio State Buckeyes. His recruitment reopened Nov. 1, the day Florida State fired Mike Norvell and handed the program to interim coach Rick Stockstill. The LSU Tigers, his hometown school, moved first, hosting Miles for an unofficial visit Nov. 7 and an official visit the following weekend. Missouri extended its offer later in November and brought him to Columbia for an official visit last weekend. NEWS: Four-star RB Jayden Miles has flipped his commitment from Florida State to Missouri, @247Sports has learned. Story: https://t.co/yX7jB1QzaU https://t.co/AmrIOX3M5C — Kolby Crawford (@kolby_crawford) November 26, 2026 Sep 21, 2024; Tallahassee, Florida, USA; Florida State Seminoles head coach Mike Norvell and associate head coach Odell Haggins high-five after winning against the California Golden Bears at Doak S. Campbell Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images Both of Missouri’s moves landed while Florida State was still searching for a permanent head coach. The Seminoles hired Georgia defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann on Nov. 23, after Missouri’s official visit had already taken place. By then, the program that had held his commitment for five months had gone 22 days without a full-time head coach to make its case. 247Sports ranks Miles as the No. 17 running back nationally and the No. 13 prospect in Louisiana, while the 247Sports Composite, which blends the major recruiting services, places him No. 27 at the position. His commitment arrived less than a week before the early signing period opens on Dec. 2. Florida State’s running back problem now stretches into 2027 Schumann’s first 2027 class holds 13 commitments, none at running back, and sits No. 70 in the 247Sports team rankings with the signing window about to open. Florida State has also played this season without its top five preseason running backs, which is how Parks ended up carrying the full load against NC State. Schumann now needs help at the position on the current depth chart and on the recruiting board at the same time, and the board just lost the one back it had. Missouri, meanwhile, comes away with its first flip of the 2027 cycle. Miles becomes the Tigers’ second running back commitment in the class, joining four-star Kingston Miles, which gives Missouri two four-star backs who share a last name heading into signing week. LSU had Miles on campus twice in November, including an official visit one weekend before Missouri’s, and he still picked a program
