item.title: What DJ Jacobs’ family said about Ohio State visits before five-star EDGE’s decommitment
item.description: The highest-rated player in the Ohio State Buckeyes’ 2027 recruiting class backed off his commitment on Thanksgiving, two days before the Buckeyes host the Michigan Wolverines and six days before the early signing period opens. Five-star edge rusher David “DJ” Jacobs of Blessed Trinity Catholic in Roswell, Georgia, confirmed the decision Thursday to Rivals’ Hayes Fawcett , who lists him as the No. 1 recruit in the class. Jacobs had been committed since Dec. 29, 2025, when he picked Ohio State live on CBS Sports HQ over finalists the Miami Hurricanes and Texas A&M Aggies. When DJ showed up at a Georgia Bulldogs home game against Western Kentucky in September, his father, former Georgia defensive lineman David Jacobs, described the trip as a visit for younger brother Dawson, a 2028 defensive line prospect, and drew a firm line around DJ’s own travel. BREAKING: Five-Star Plus+ EDGE David “DJ” Jacobs has Decommitted from Ohio State, he tells me for @Rivals He’s ranked as the No. 1 Recruit in the 2027 Class https://t.co/IhcljUfXUf https://t.co/W1BnswLfaB — Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) November 26, 2026 Ryan Day’s Bold Claim of First and Second Rounders Reflects How Ohio State Gets Down, Says National Analyst (Imagn Images) “The only visits that DJ has set up are to Ohio State. He went up for the first game. He’s going back to Ohio State for the Oregon game. He’s also going back to Ohio State for the Michigan game. The only visits he’s got set up are for those three games. Everything else is a visit for Dawson,” David Jacobs told DawgNation’s Jeff Sentell. DJ made the first two of those trips. The second came on Nov. 7, when the Oregon Ducks climbed out of a two-touchdown hole with 38 straight points and left Ohio Stadium with a 41-28 win. The Michigan game was the third, and 247Sports’ Tom Loy reported that Jacobs is no longer making that trip. Both brothers were at Neyland Stadium when the Tennessee Volunteers hosted the Texas Longhorns on Sept. 26, and both were back in Knoxville when the Vols played the LSU Tigers on Nov. 21. For a fall the family described as Dawson’s recruiting tour, DJ’s most recent campus stop was Tennessee, and his next one in Columbus is now off. Six days separate Jacobs from the early signing period Miami, one of the two finalists Ohio State beat out last winter, brought Jacobs back to campus in April. Georgia carries the family tie through his father’s playing days in Athens, and Tennessee has had him inside Neyland Stadium twice this fall. Ohio State can still recruit him as an uncommitted prospect, and nothing requires Jacobs to sign during the December window, which runs from Wednesday through Friday, Dec. 4. Prospects who wait can put pen to paper in the February period instead, and the Buckeyes would have to make that pitch without the Michigan game visit the family had circled in September. Whichever program gets his signature lands an edge rusher who finished his junior season with 102 tackles, 24 tackles for loss

item.title: Chelsea’s chances of landing £100m dream midfield target in January rated by the Athletic
item.description: Chelsea’s chances of landing £100m dream midfield target in January rated by the Athletic Chelsea’s interest in Alex Scott is well reported – but how likely are they to actually be able to land him in January? If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. The Athletic’s “Deal Sheet” summary of Chelsea’s potential transfer business says that the Blues could sign players in a number of positions. But there’s nowhere with more need than central midfield, and there’s no player more heavily linked than Alex Scott of Bournemouth. Fans shouldn’t get too excited, however. The article claims that Chelsea are “wary they could face competition” for the midfielder and “believe they may have to wait until the summer.” Chelsea face tough battle to land in-demand central midfielder Alex Scott (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Earlier in the year it felt like the fact that Bournemouth had made a slow start made it possible they would want to hold on to their key player until the summer to ensure they stayed clear of relegation. Now the opposite is true – they’re on a superb run and may instead want to keep him to see just how high in the table they can finish. The Blues also aren’t offering a very tempting destination right now. There’s bound to be competition from other teams, and another year of chaos at Chelsea might not be what a player pushing to get into the England team wants to sign up for. In other news… Emmanuel Emegha is in the mix for tonight’s game and we expect him to start. Xabi Alonso had some words about what he can offer the team. The injury report for tonight’s game has one vital starter confirmed as back – but two regulars will still be missing.

item.title: Texas Tech follows 2025 blueprint into final Big 12 championship game against unbeaten Utah
item.description: The Texas Tech Red Raiders opened 2025 with six straight wins, dropped their seventh game on the road and did not lose again on the way to the program’s first Big 12 title. The 2026 team has followed that route almost step for step, and it now ends at the Big 12 Championship Game against the No. 2 Utah Utes on Dec. 4. Tech locked up its spot Thursday night in Lubbock with a 48-27 win over the TCU Horned Frogs, a result that also ended the BYU Cougars’ hopes of returning to Arlington. Thomas Castellanos completed 20 of 25 passes for a career-high 374 yards and three touchdowns, two of them in a four-play span late in the first half. Oct 11, 2025; Lubbock, Texas, USA; A general view of Texas Tech Red Raiders helmets in the second half on the bench during the game against the Kansas Jayhawks at Jones AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Michael C. Johnson-Imagn Images TCU, playing its first game since firing Sonny Dykes on Sunday, led 10-0 after one quarter while Tech went three-and-out on its first two possessions. The Red Raiders outscored the Frogs 48-17 from there, turning two second-quarter turnovers into 10 points and scoring touchdowns on their first three drives of the second half. After a 6-0 start this fall, Tech lost 37-24 at the Cincinnati Bearcats on Oct. 24. The 2025 team took its only regular-season loss in the same spot, 26-22 at the Arizona State Sun Devils in game seven, and answered by winning its last five regular-season games before beating BYU for the conference crown. This group has now won five straight since Cincinnati, finishing 11-1 overall and 8-1 in league play. Texas Tech gets one shot at the last Big 12 title game The Big 12 announced that this year’s game will be the final edition, with the College Football Playoff expanding to 24 teams in 2027 and the league’s automatic bid moving to its regular-season champion. Whoever wins in Arlington will be the last team to lift that trophy. Utah is unbeaten in Morgan Scalley’s first season as head coach at his alma mater. The Utes clinched their spot with a win at TCU on Nov. 21 and entered that game riding a 16-game winning streak, the longest active run in FBS. They also beat BYU in their rivalry game on Nov. 7, and the Cougars entered this week as the only team besides Tech still alive for the second spot, needing a win over Cincinnati and a Tech loss. A win would make Tech the first team to win consecutive Big 12 title games since the Oklahoma Sooners won four straight from 2017 to 2020. It would also make Joey McGuire’s program the final champion of a game the league first played in 1996, in what will be its 25th and last edition. item.title: Gaming The System: IU Indy's hot start
item.description: If you're unfamiliar with IU Indy (formerly and forever in my heart known as IUPUI), Ben Howlett and The System, let me introduce you. The System means running. A lot. Howlett presses the entire game, sprints out in transition, and frequently runs full hockey-style five-player line changes to keep his guys fresh. I recommend this piece by Sam Federman from last summer for a deeper dive, but the ten-second version above should get the point across. The System debuted at the D-I level last year, but it doesn't come from Howlett. He played and then coached at West Liberty University under the brains behind the operation, the legendary Jim Crutchfield. Howlett, though, was the first to workshop it at the top level of the college game. In year one, there were signs of life, but they were relatively few and far between. The Jaguars went 7-25 (3-17 Horizon League), a three-win decrease from the one and only season under Paul Corsaro. They finished 317th at KenPom, an improvement over their 354th spot in preseason projections but nevertheless a mild drop from 312th under Corsaro. So far this year, it's been a different story. The Jags have four wins in seven games and have jumped from 316th preseason in KenPom to 275th in the season's first month. They led Penn State for nearly 25 minutes before ultimately losing by seven. They've won three of four against the four D-I teams within 100 spots of them at KenPom, either way, including a win over UT-Martin, an OVC favorite. And Howlett has accomplished it by doing something he may have never thought he'd do: slow down. Not all the way, but enough. The changes by the numbers Don't get me wrong, this team still runs. If you saw the Jags last season and you've watched them this November, it probably looks nearly indiscernible play by play. They still press full court for 40 minutes. The hockey subs still come into play. Their games are still track meets: in seven contests, neither IU Indy nor their opponent has scored below 70 points even once. But a look at the underlying numbers shows some distinct changes, most of which have had a positive effect early on. First and foremost is the pace. The 25-26 iteration of the Jaguars played 74.6 possessions per game, the highest in the country. item.content:encoded: If you're unfamiliar with IU Indy (formerly and forever in my heart known as IUPUI), Ben Howlett and The System, let me introduce you. The System means running. A lot. Howlett presses the entire game, sprints out in transition, and frequently runs full hockey-style five-player line changes to keep his guys fresh. I recommend this piece by Sam Federman from last summer for a deeper dive, but the ten-second version above should get the point across. The System debuted at the D-I level last year, but it doesn't come from Howlett. He played and then coached at West Liberty University under the brains behind the operation, the legendary Jim Crutchfield. Howlett, though, was the first to workshop it at the top level of the college game. In year one, there were signs of life, but they were relatively few and far between. The Jaguars went 7-25 (3-17 Horizon League), a three-win decrease from the one and only season under Paul Corsaro. They finished 317th at KenPom, an improvement over their 354th spot in preseason projections but nevertheless a mild drop from 312th under Corsaro. So far this year, it's been a different story. The Jags have four wins in seven games and have jumped from 316th preseason in KenPom to 275th in the season's first month. They led Penn State for nearly 25 minutes before ultimately losing by seven. They've won three of four against the four D-I teams within 100 spots of them at KenPom, either way, including a win over UT-Martin, an OVC favorite. And Howlett has accomplished it by doing something he may have never thought he'd do: slow down. Not all the way, but enough. The changes by the numbers Don't get me wrong, this team still runs. If you saw the Jags last season and you've watched them this November, it probably looks nearly indiscernible play by play. They still press full court for 40 minutes. The hockey subs still come into play. Their games are still track meets: in seven contests, neither IU Indy nor their opponent has scored below 70 points even once. But a look at the underlying numbers shows some distinct changes, most of which have had a positive effect early on. First and foremost is the pace. The 25-26 iteration of the Jaguars played 74.6 possessions per game, the highest in the country. This season, they're at 70.6 possessions, an unremarkable number that has them in the 67th %ile for pace. But if they're not backing off the press, what's causing it? First of all, the Jags have made strides on the offensive glass. They get three more misses back per game, despite taking almost two fewer shots. That's boosted their offense while slowing the game down possession-wise. The stat that jumps out most, though, and that points directly to the slower pace, is how much of IU Indy's games are played in transition. Last year, it allowed a stunning 17% of opponent FGA to come in transition while taking 17.5% of its shots on the run. This year, offensive transition sits at 14.6%, while transition FGA defense sits at 14.3%, up from 11.9% before its most recent game against William & Mary. In transition efficiency, the numbers have gotten worse on offense but improved defensively. Last year, the Jags allowed an NCAA-worst 69.2% on transition FGA. This year, it's 67.8% but was 65.2% before the W&M game, still bad but survivably so. Overall, the defense has been much stiffer inside. Year-over-year, Jags opponents are shooting 8.5% worse at the rim and taking 3% more mid-range FGA than a year ago, when they forced the fewest of any team in the country. The 3-point defense has also been significantly better, but that may be attributable to variance. IU Indy defensive heat maps, 25-26 left and 26-27 right IU Indy's improvement is more noticeable on the defensive end, but it's been better offensively too. The change is attributable to a strategic alteration of the shot diet. The Cats are taking threes at a rate about 10% higher than last year's already-above-median 42.7%. Their 52.6% 3Pr so far is in the top 20 nationally. While that creates variance that could bug them game-to-game, it has paid off impressively so far, putting the math more in their favor while opening up opportunities to offensive rebound and forcing at least one defender back to prevent so many transition opportunities. The other change has come at the free throw line. No team took fewer free throws last year than the Jaguars, whose 21.1% FTA rate was more than 3% lower than anyone else. That number has risen to 33.3%, around the 36th percentile nationally. They're not overpowering, but it's a marked improvement over a year ago. All told, the Jaguars have posted a 9.3 net rating so far, per CBB Analytics, compared to -6.3 a year ago. Now let's look at who's driving the strong start. The players behind the numbers As you may expect in The System, there isn't really a star. Because of how much running this team does, they have 11 guys who have played 60+ minutes in the first seven games. All told, the Jags run out 98 bench minutes a night, or 49% of total minutes, a top 15 mark in the country. The production mirrors it, with 40 points per game (right around 49%) coming from the reserves, similarly a top 15 ranking. If you're looking for a place to start, Billy Smith is as good as any. The fifth-year transfer from Chattanooga leads the team in scoring at 14.3 PPG, and he's doing it by simply not missing. Billy Smith shooting splits This is what the shooting chart spits out for Smith. He's making 67% of his twos (and he's made 12 of 13 at the rim thus far) and a ridiculous 46.9% from three despite nearly three of every four shot attempts coming from beyond the arc. In the second half of games, he's rocking a cool 80/50 split from the floor. Oh yeah, he's also come off the bench in all seven games. The two returners are Kameron Tinsley and Reece Hagy. Tinsley is the third-leading scorer and second-best three-point shooter behind Smith, making 39% of his six attempts per game. Hagy, meanwhile, is scoring just 1.7 points per game in under 12 minutes a night, but has a nearly 3:1 A:TO ratio and is swiping away a 2.1% steal rate, which ranks in the 65th percentile. If you're into on/off splits, Peyton Heiss is your guy. When Heiss is on the floor, the offense may not shoot as many free throws, but they make more shots, take more threes, and pass the ball much better without turning it over more. Defensively, they're nearly 13 points better when the 6'4" guard is out there defending versus riding pine. Peyton Heiss on/off splits Part of what makes this team so great is that anyone can beat you on any night. But if Coach Howlett can keep leaning on his vets and returners, this team will continue to shine. What this start means At the top of the article, you may remember I mentioned that IU Indy was up to 275th in KenPom and thought that sounded unimpressive. In comparison to the rest of the country, it largely is. However, it's important to contextualize where this program is. A 275th-place finish in KenPom would be the best since 2021 and just the second time this side of COVID finishing inside the top 300, a stretch that includes four different coaches. Within the Horizon League, the Jaguars sit 10th out of 12 teams right now by KenPom rank. However, there are a ridiculous SIX teams in a 20-team range from the Horizon, with IU Indy sitting last of those six. If it can filter its way to the top of this group, that would put the Jags 5th in the league, an achievement IU Indy has not completed since making the move from the Summit League in 2017-18. Its best finish was 6th place in a 10-team Horizon in its first year. Even if IU Indy gets to, say, 8th in the league, that would be its second-best finish ever as a Horizon member. The Jaguars haven't played a .500 season or better in conference play since 2015-16, in the Summit. There's a real path to do so here and Ben Howlett will have his boys ready and running in pursuit of it.

item.title: He's back! Rodri is training with Barça and has Riazor in his sights 🔙
item.description: He's back! Rodri is training with Barça and has Riazor in his sights 🔙 The Madrid-born midfielder trained as normal alongside the rest of his teammates at the Ciutat Esportiva on Friday. Having recovered from his hamstring injury, he will be available for Hansi Flick for Sunday's trip to Riazor. Good news for Barça's midfield. Rodri Hernández completed Friday's training session with the squad, confirming that his recovery is on track. The Spanish holding midfielder has shaken off the right hamstring injury he suffered earlier this month against Aston Villa in the Champions League. A key piece in Hansi Flick's plans The Spain captain's return is a huge relief for Hansi Flick, who gets his midfield orchestrator back just as the fixture list becomes congested. Although the coaching staff remain extremely cautious to avoid a setback, all signs point to the Madrid native being included in the squad travelling to A Coruña. The aim is clear: to give him valuable minutes against Deportivo at Riazor this Sunday (16:15) to build match sharpness ahead of next week's demanding clash with Atlético de Madrid. Barça's injury update The morning session in Sant Joan Despí also brought other important team news. Lamine Yamal also returned to group training after overcoming minor ankle discomfort. Meanwhile, Andreas Christensen and Marc Bernal trained separately from the group, while Fermín López is ruled out of the trip to Riazor through suspension. This article was translated into English by Artificial Intelligence. You can read the original version in 🇪🇸 here.

item.title: Jamie Overton tears through Australia as England claim emphatic win in third T20
item.description: Jamie Overton bullied Australia into submission at the Gabba, taking five for 12 as England claimed another T20 walkover against their biggest rivals. Having squared the series 1-1 with a dominant showing on the Gold Coast, Overton carried the tourists to a seven-wicket DLS victory to complete a Queensland double in Brisbane. The 6ft 5in quick gave Australia the runaround with his pace and bounce, gutting their batting line-up with a four-over spell that contained just seven scoring shots and a solitary boundary. All out for 108 in less than 17 overs, they were all but beaten at the halfway stage. There were three separate rain delays in a disjointed chase, but the result was never in doubt as Aneurin Donald’s 31 and an unbeaten 33 from Jordan Cox eased England to a recalculated target of 93 with 43 balls remaining. The evening was Overton’s, though, as he claimed the best ever bowling figures in a T20 between the sides, England’s previous best of four for 24 set by Jon Lewis in their first ever meeting in the format 21 years ago. There was no sign of an Australian implosion at the start of their innings, with six sixes sailing over the ropes as they passed 50 inside five overs. Sam Curran was hit for easily the biggest by Jake Fraser-McGurk as his first visit went for 16. England leaned on Liam Dawson to exert some control and he obliged, hustling through two tidy powerplay overs and persuading both Mitch Marsh and Sam Harper to pick out mid-on. Overton was the catcher on both occasions, but his evening was only just getting started. The score was 64 for two when the Surrey man entered the attack for the seventh over and 97 for seven when he took his cap at the end of the 13th. He took care of Fraser-McGurk with his second ball, failing to clear Tom Banton at long on, and then went after the power-hitter Tim David. Liam Dawson (second right) made the first breakthroughs for England (Tertius Pickard/AP). Having rapped him on the forearm with a sharp bouncer, Overton bided his time as David received treatment then dismissed him via a top-edged pull off the next delivery. He should have had two in two when Joel Davies was juggled by Adil Rashid at backward point, but a short ball soon accounted for the outmatched all-rounder. Australia were increasingly unsure of how to play Overton, unsettled by his zippy bounce and too keen to step away to leg, and he finished his spell with an emphatic double-wicket maiden. Back to his task after putting down a return catch that rattled his thumb and needed the attention of the physio, he had Nikhil Chaudhary caught in the deep attempting a shot requiring more muscle than he could muster and signed off by taking Ben Dwarshuis’ outside edge. Australia’s tail barely threatened a fightback. Dawson took a third, while Rashid breezed through four overs, Mitch Owen was ran out messily and Curran blew through last man Billy Stanlake. The evening was Overton’s, though, as he claimed the best ever bowling figures in a T20 between the sides, England’s previous best of four for 24 set by Jon Lewis in their first ever meeting in the format 21 years ago. Overton was the catcher on both occasions, but his evening was only just getting started. The score was 64 for two when the Surrey man entered the attack for the seventh over and 97 for seven when he took his cap at the end of the 13th. He took care of Fraser-McGurk with his second ball, failing to clear Tom Banton at long on, and then went after the power-hitter Tim David. Liam Dawson (second right) made the first breakthroughs for England (Tertius Pickard/AP). Having rapped him on the forearm with a sharp bouncer, Overton bided his time as David received treatment then dismissed him via a top-edged pull off the next delivery. He should have had two in two when Joel Davies was juggled by Adil Rashid at backward point, but a short ball soon accounted for the outmatched all-rounder. Australia were increasingly unsure of how to play Overton, unsettled by his zippy bounce and too keen to step away to leg, and he finished his spell with an emphatic double-wicket maiden. Back to his task after putting down a return catch that rattled his thumb and needed the attention of the physio, he had Nikhil Chaudhary caught in the deep attempting a shot requiring more muscle than he could muster and signed off by taking Ben Dwarshuis’ outside edge. Australia’s tail barely threatened a fightback. Dawson took a third, while Rashid breezed through four overs, Mitch Owen was ran out messily and Curran blew through last man Billy Stanlake. A slender chase of 109 would not have worried England’s all-Welsh opening pair, having put on 151 in the previous match, but Phil Salt was an early casualty when he failed to get hold of Riley Meredith and popped a soft catch to cover. Donald was soon back in the swing of things, though, taking a like to Stanlake on the latter’s first T20 outing in seven years. At one stage he took 22 off a five-ball sequence from the tall seamer, pulling and cutting with gusto. Harry Brook hammered his fourth ball for a flat six over cover, suggesting England were in a hurry to get things done, before rain intervened. Aneurin Donald hit 32 off 13 balls (Tertius Pickard/AP). Meredith did his best to make a game of it after the restart, dismissing Brook and Donald in the space of three balls before another interruption. The winning line was revised down to 98 in 17 overs, then 93 in 16 as the weather made for a frustrating finish. Cox made hay, hitting five fours and a six in just 14 balls to end it for good off just 8.5 overs.

item.title: Fury cleared to fight Joshua after medical checks
item.description: Tyson Fury has won 36 of his 39 fights as a professional [Getty Images] Tyson Fury has been medically cleared to fight Anthony Joshua in December after the bout was put in jeopardy by claims of a schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury, 38, spoke of his mental health struggles in a Netflix documentary which was released on Friday, with his wife, Paris, saying he had been diagnosed with schizophrenia. But Paris has since retracted that statement, saying he "doesn't have this condition" and Netflix have edited the remarks out of their film. The British Boxing Board of Control told BBC Sport: "Tyson Fury has been cleared to box on 11 December." Fury faces Joshua in a long overdue all-British heavyweight contest at Cardiff's Principality Stadium in the early hours of 12 December. More to follow. item.title: Nico Paz’s stance on potential Man Utd move and Real Madrid return revealed
item.description: Nico Paz’s stance on potential Man Utd move and Real Madrid return revealed According to The Athletic , Como star Nico Paz does not currently favour rejoining Real Madrid this summer, and Manchester United may not be his first choice, especially if the Red Devils don’t qualify for the Champions League. Como star Nico Paz inevitably continues to grab headlines worldwide thanks to his fantastic performances under Cesc Fabregas. MILAN, ITALY – NOVEMBER 08: Nico Paz of Como 1907 runs with the ball during the Serie A match between FC Internazionale and Como 1907 at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on November 08, 2026 in Milan, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Paz has six goals and eight assists in 16 appearances across all competitions this season, and Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him for €80m in the summer. According to The Athletic, however, the Argentine currently does not favour a return to the Spanish capital. “This stance might alter if he is assured of a prominent role — that has not been the case,” The Athletic clarifies. According to the report, Manchester United see the Argentine as a potential replacement for Bruno Fernandes, whose contract expires at the end of the season. ITALY – OCTOBER 21: Nico Paz of Como 1907 is challenged by Andrey Santos of Manchester United during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at Giuseppe Sinigaglia Stadium on October 21, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) The Athletic explains that the Red Devils “may not be Nico Paz’s first-choice destination, and Champions League qualification is a major factor.” Manchester United saw Nico Paz’s quality firsthand in October, when the Argentine scored two goals and provided one assist in Como’s 4-1 victory in a Champions League match at the Stadio Sinigaglia. This is Nico Paz’s third season in Como. The Azzurri re-signed him from Real Madrid last summer for €60m.

item.title: Patriots Have Another Reason To Be Concerned About Buffalo Following Thanksgiving
item.description: Patriots Have Another Reason To Be Concerned About Buffalo Following Thanksgiving originally appeared on NESN . Add NESN as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New England Patriots received another reminder Thursday night of just how difficult it could be to challenge the Buffalo Bills for AFC East supremacy. Buffalo defeated the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 on Thanksgiving, improving to 10-1 and extending its winning streak to seven games. Tyler Bass delivered the decisive points with a 57-yard field goal as time expired. What made Buffalo's victory particularly interesting from New England's perspective wasn't necessarily the final score. The Bills managed to defeat one of the AFC's most dangerous teams despite receiving relatively little production from their most recognizable offensive player. That should concern every team hoping to challenge Buffalo during the remainder of the season. Buffalo Doesn't Always Need Josh Allen To Be Spectacular Allen completed just 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards and threw two interceptions against Kansas City. Those aren't the numbers football fans ordinarily associate with one of the NFL's premier quarterbacks, particularly during his games against Patrick Mahomes. Nevertheless, Buffalo found another way to win. BILLS WIN!!!!!!!!!!!!! @MandT_Bank | #KCvsBUF https://t.co/y23fz9iBod — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 James Cook rushed for 117 yards and a touchdown, while Buffalo's defense prevented Kansas City from establishing consistent offensive momentum. Bass eventually converted two field goals from beyond 50 yards in the fourth quarter. The ability to win games without exceptional quarterback production represents an important characteristic of championship contenders. Buffalo demonstrated Thursday that it doesn't necessarily need Allen to produce several spectacular plays to defeat quality opposition. MORE: Patriots’ Final Seven Games Leave Little Room For A Slow Start New England Can Learn Something From Buffalo's Victory The Patriots have their own challenges to navigate as the season enters its final stretch. Establishing a dependable running game, generating defensive stops and receiving consistent special teams contributions become particularly important when quarterback production is uncertain. Buffalo's Thanksgiving performance offered an interesting example of how those elements can work together. The Bills didn't need to win an offensive shootout against Mahomes, and they didn't allow Allen's turnovers to determine the outcome. New England's long-term objective involves building a roster capable of competing with Buffalo on a regular basis. Thursday's result demonstrated that accomplishing that requires considerably more than simply finding a franchise quarterback. The Bills have become a difficult team to defeat even when their biggest star struggles. That's an important standard for Mike Vrabel and the Patriots to pursue as they continue developing their own championship aspirati

item.title: Ipswich Women sign Ademiluyi for record fee
item.description: Ademiluyi had been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February [Getty Images] Ipswich Town Women have confirmed the permanent signing of England youth international Princess Ademiluyi for an undisclosed club record fee. The 20-year-old forward has been on loan at the Tractor Girls from NWSL side Gotham FC since February and has agreed a three-and-a-half year deal at the WSL2 side. Ademiluyi has been capped by England at under-19 and under-20 level, and has been called up for the under-23 side for the first time ahead of their internationals against Belgium and Portugal next week. "I have really made a home for myself in Suffolk and I am so excited to continue building what has been a positive start to the season for us as a group," she told the club's website. "The players, staff and supporters have all been brilliant with me since I arrived and I can't wait to see where this club can go and to continue making more memories together." Ipswich Town chairman Mark Ashton said: "Signing Princess on a permanent basis has been a real priority for us and completing such a significant deal as this highlights the club's ongoing commitment to reach the top level of the game. "This is a statement signing for the club, with further announcements to come in due course as we reaffirm our commitment to our women's set-up in both the short and long-term." Ademiluyi started her career at WSL side West Ham in 2023 before moving to US-based Gotham and is Ipswich's top scorer so far in 2026-27, with four goals. The Tractor Girls finished ninth in WSL2 last season following promotion to the second tier in 2025, and were in the fourth tier as recently as 2021. Under the management of former men's team player David Wright, appointed to the role in April, the Blues are third after eight games this season, three points behind leaders Newcastle United. Ipswich on 'inevitable' path to WSL - Boswell A statement of intent - analysis Ademiluyi has played an important role in helping the Tractor Girls transform from relegation candidates to title contenders. She made an immediate impact on joining in February, scoring goals against Durham and Birmingham City to help secure the team's survival in WSL2. The forward has continued to find the net this season, and won the WSL2 player of the month award for October. There is a growing feeling within the women's game that the Blues will be playing at the highest level in the not too distant future and securing a proven goalscorer whose stock is also rising on the international stage will only strengthen that train of thought. Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

item.title: ‘FIRE THE ENTIRE STAFF!’ NFL Pundits and Famous Fans Erupt After Cowboys’ Epic Thanksgiving Implosion
item.description: (Screengrab via Fox) Stephen A. Smith was reduced to tears of laughter and Skip Bayless declared himself finished with the Dallas Cowboys as the Philadelphia Eagles pulled off the biggest comeback in NFL Thanksgiving history on Thursday. The sports world erupted after Philadelphia overturned a staggering 21-point deficit to beat its bitter NFC East rival 39-38, with kicker Jake Elliott drilling a 59-yard field goal with just seconds on the clock. The architect of Dallas’s humiliation was Eagles backup quarterback Joe Milton III , who was cut from the Cowboys in August but returned to haunt his old team with a sensational second-half comeback. Smith, a longtime tormentor of Cowboys fans, could barely contain himself in a video posted to X, wheezing with laughter as he mocked Dallas for losing to its former third-string quarterback. “Just when you think it can’t get worse!!” he wrote. But Milton, filling in for the injured Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts , torched his former team for 331 passing yards and three touchdowns as Philadelphia mounted a ferocious fightback. The Eagles’ turnaround gathered pace in a frantic fourth quarter when Ty Robinson blocked a Dallas punt and Kenny Moore II returned it for a touchdown. Dallas briefly restored its two-touchdown cushion through a Dak Prescott rushing score, but Milton answered with a 15-yard touchdown run before finding WR Makai Lemon for another score to bring Philadelphia within two points. The Cowboys then squandered a chance to put the contest beyond reach when Brandon Aubrey missed a 40-yard field goal. With less than a minute remaining, Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer gambled on fourth-and-one rather than punt. Prescott was promptly sacked for a nine-yard loss, handing Philadelphia possession near midfield. A costly pass interference penalty against Dallas safety Markquese Bell then helped set up Elliott’s improbable 59-yard winner. Former Eagles stars were celebrating. Terrell Owens seized the opportunity to taunt Cowboys owner Jerry Jones while ex-Philadelphia center Jason Kelce branded Milton “Bazooka Joe”: Fly Eagles Fly!!!! @Eagles Happy Thanksgiving Jerry Jones!!! Ya’ll told me last week Titans scoring 30 was a fluke. What about 39 2 the Eagles with a bck up Qb. That out played your MVP candidate Qb? Eagles haven’t scored more than 24 pts in gm this yr. Your defensive personnel isn’t good. That’s the issue not the DC. — shannon sharpe (@ShannonSharpe) November 27, 2026 Joe Milton — Field Yates (@FieldYates) November 26, 2026 Joe Milton reminds me of blend of Tom Brady and Dan Marino — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) November 27, 2026 It was ESPN analyst Mina Kimes , however, who delivered perhaps the most cutting verdict on Dallas’s Thanksgiving disaster: “The 2026 Cowboys are performance art.” The 2026 Cowboys are performance art — Mina Kimes (@minakimes) November 27, 2026 The victory improves Philadelphia to 4-7, while Dallas slipped to 5-7. item.title: Tyson Fury ‘cleared’ to fight Anthony Joshua after clarification on schizophrenia diagnosis
item.description: Tyson Fury has reportedly been medically cleared to box Anthony Joshua , after confusion around a possible schizophrenia diagnosis. Fury is scheduled to face his fellow British heavyweight on 11 December , as the pair headline at Cardiff’s Principallity stadium in a fight years in the making. However, the bout appeared to be under threat this week, as quotes from Tyson Fury – a new Netflix documentary – did the rounds. The quotes saw Fury’s wife Paris suggesting that the boxer was once diagnosed with schizophrenia. Tyson Fury in 2026 (PA) That prompted Robert Smith, general secretary of the British Boxing Board of Control (BBBofC), to tell the BBC: “We are in the process of dealing with the matter, but if there are any medical issues we wouldn’t let anyone box. It doesn’t matter if it’s Tyson Fury or not, it could be anybody. I’m fairly confident he will be absolutely fine. We’re dealing with it now and we’ll have an answer very shortly.” Paris soon released a statement that read : “I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary. I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.” Meanwhile, Netflix said: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.” The film was released on Friday, and the scene in question had been reported on earlier this week, following preview screenings earlier in November . Friday also brought an update from journalist Gareth A Davies, who tweeted: “Tyson Fury’s medicals were all cleared by the Boxing Board on Thursday evening. His promoter was informed Friday morning. The notion that Fury vs Anthony Joshua would have been cancelled on mental health grounds is extremely unlikely.” The Independent has contacted the BBBofC for comment. Fury will finally face Anthony Joshua on 11 December (PA Wire) Fury vs Joshua is a fight that has been discussed for the best part of a decade. The pair even signed to fight each other during Covid, only for Deontay Wilder to threaten legal action and force a trilogy bout with Fury instead. At the time, Fury and Joshua held all the major heavyweight belts between them, but Joshua would lose the unified titles in his next fight. The 37-year-old has not held a world title since. Meanwhile, Fury, 38, retained the WBC belt until 2024, but he will similarly enter his clash with “AJ” without a world title. The vacant WBA Super belt will be on the line, however, when the heavyweights collide. This week brought confirmation that the fight will actually begin at 1.30am on 12 December, with increased stewarding, police presence, and travel options around the Welsh capital.

item.title: Mike Tomlin explains how Steelers owner will handle Mike McCarthy
item.description: Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images, Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images, Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images The Pittsburgh Steelers have epitomised dysfunction this week. After Aaron Rodgers was benched and made inactive, the four-time NFL MVP called into The Pat McAfee Show and went scorched earth on head coach Mike McCarthy. The Steelers promptly released Rodgers, and on Thanksgiving night, the man who helmed McCarthy’s job as Pittsburgh’s coach for 19 seasons weighed in. Former Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin, who now serves as an analyst for NBC’s Football Night in America, didn’t mince words on Thursday night, calling the situation “a dumpster fire” and admitting that he was upset and saddened by the whole saga. “Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy” Tomlin also explained how Steelers owner Art Rooney II will handle the situation and how his process is different than most of the modern team owners around the league. “Art is a guy that’s not a hedge fund guy that bought a football team. He’s not a, you know, artificial intelligence guy that bought a football team,” Tomlin said. ” This is a family business. It’s generational. Any advice or thought process in that way, I imagine he just says, ‘What would my dad do?’ or, ‘What would my grandfather do?’ Their mode of operation is time-tested. It’s generational. And so I doubt very, very seriously that he called anyone for outside advice.” “He was beloved” Interestingly, Tomlin also said that while coaching Rodgers in 2025, the veteran quarterback was a wonderful presence in the locker room. “He was beloved, and I’m not over-exaggerating that,” Tomlin said. “He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture, to be engaged with teammates.” “And particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, et cetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way,” Tomlin continued. All in all, Tomlin is saddened by the way things ended. “Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers, and just on the macro level, whether it’s organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum, those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.” The post Mike Tomlin explains how Steelers owner will handle Mike McCarthy appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: Confirmed: Brahim Diaz signs new contract with Real Madrid until 2031
item.description: Confirmed: Brahim Diaz signs new contract with Real Madrid until 2031 The series of contract renewals continues at Real Madrid as the club have now announced that Brahim Diaz has penned a new long-term deal until 2031. “Real Madrid CF and Brahim Diaz have agreed to extend the contract of our player, who is now tied to the club until June 30, 2031,” the club statement read. Signed from Manchester City in the January transfer window of 2019, Brahim has grown into a valuable squad player at Real Madrid. After initially finding it hard to break into the team, the Moroccan star spent three seasons away on loan at AC Milan, before returning in 2023. Since then, he has become a key player under different managers even though he has been unable to establish himself as a regular starter in the team. So far in his Real Madrid career, Brahim has made 173 appearances, scoring 22 and assisting 34 goals. In the process, the versatile attacker has won won seven titles at the club – 1 Champions League, 1 Club World Cup, 1 UEFA Super Cup, 2 La Liga titles, and 2 Spanish Super Cups. While minutes have been hard to come by this season as well, Brahim remains committed to Real Madrid and has renewed for five more years until 2031. Brahim’s renewal follows after Real Madrid also secured the futures of Arda Guler, Aurelien Tchouameni, and Thibaut Courtois over the last week. Jude Bellingham and Federico Valverde are expected to be next in line to sign long-term renewals.

item.title: Sam Roush: Bears Rookie Tight End Earns Bigger Role After Career-Best Game
item.description: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - FEBRUARY 27: Sam Roush of the Stanford Cardinal participates in a drill during the 2026 NFL Scouting Combine at Lucas Oil Stadium on February 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty S am Roush: Bears rookie tight end and 2026 third-round pick out of Stanford, did not dominate the Thanksgiving Day highlight reels in Detroit, yet he quietly delivered the most impactful performance of his young NFL career. Catching all five of his targets for 31 yards in Chicago Bears ’s thrilling 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions , the 6-foot-6, 267-pound tight end stepped directly into an emergency workload and helped keep the Bears’ offense moving. While 31 receiving yards looks modest on a box score that featured 74 total points, it marked a major step forward for a rookie who had never logged more than two receptions in a single contest prior to Week 12. A Reliable Option When the Bears Needed One Chicago’s tight end depth chart faced an immediate crisis early in Thursday’s contest when starter Colston Loveland went down with a knee injury after a Lions defender rolled into his lower left leg on a run-blocking snap. With veteran Cole Kmet already out for the remainder of the season following a Week 7 knee injury against New England, the Bears suddenly had to lean heavily on Roush and fellow reserve Stephen Carlson. Roush answered the call without hesitation. Converting every single pass thrown his way , the No. 69 overall draft pick became one of quarterback Caleb Williams’ most dependable underneath outlets, showcasing the physicality and sure hands that drew Chicago’s front office to him in April. One sequence in particular captured why the coaching staff trusts him in heavy traffic. On an 11-yard reception, Roush lowered his shoulder and powered straight through a would-be Lions tackler for extra yardage—the exact brand of tough, after-the-catch finishing that defined his college tape at Stanford. Drafted primarily for his inline blocking chops and physical edge, Thursday proved he can handle real passing-game volume when injuries strike. Trust Building at a Critical Spot Head coach Ben Johnson has steadily praised Roush’s weekly growth throughout his rookie campaign, noting how quickly the young tight end has grasped the nuances of Chicago’s offense. Thursday’s Thanksgiving showcase offered the clearest on-field proof yet that the staff’s long-term vision for him is taking hold. Roush is not suddenly going to morph into a high-volume vertical receiving threat, nor does Chicago’s scheme ask him to fill that role. What he can provide is a trustworthy security blanket over the middle of the field paired with rugged perimeter and inline blocking—precisely the kind of multi-purpose complementary piece Johnson’s offense thrives on. Roush ready to handle starter-level snaps Loveland’s availability remains uncertain heading into next week’s matchup against the Jacksonville Jaguars, though the mini-bye created by Thursday’s holiday kickoff gives Chicago’s medical staff a few extra days to evaluate his knee. If the second-year starter is limited or forced to sit out Week 13, Roush is squarely positioned to handle starter-level snaps. Carlson also chipped in with two catches for 30 yards against Detroit to give Williams another viable option, yet Roush’s combination of size, blocking reliability, and crisp execution makes him the natural choice to anchor the position group. For a first-year player who spent the opening two months of the season working largely in supporting packages, catching all five targets in a high-stakes divisional shootout carries real weight inside Halas Hall. The Bears now sit at 9-2 and stand alone atop the NFC North—and disciplined, unheralded performances like the one Sam Roush, Bears rookie tight end, delivered in Detroit are a big reason why. item.title: Former WWE star Braun Strowman’s in-ring return match announced
item.description: Former WWE star Braun Strowman’s in-ring return match announced appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Earlier last year, former WWE Universal Champion Braun Strowman parted ways with the promotion. Shortly after, it was reported that Strowman was released from the promotion due to higher salary demands. Later, it was also noted that WWE wanted to have him back as a part-timer. However, that never advanced. While Strowman almost stopped pursuing his in-ring career after WWE, he started his own TV show, Everything on the Menu with Braun Strowman. The first season was a major success and the show was later renewed for a second season. Now, a few months after his first in-ring return, Strowman is set to lace his boots again . Recently, Great Lakes Championship Wrestling announced on social media that Strowman will team up with Erick Redbeard, aka, Erick Rowan, against The Good Brothers (Doc Gallows and Karl Anderson) at Blizzard Brawl 21. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The above-mentioned event will take place on Dec. 5, 2026, at Potawatomi Hotel & Casino (Ballroom) in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. Strowman and Redbeard share a long history and have teamed up several times in the past during their time together in WWE. Earlier this year, Strowman also underwent surgery to drain excess fluid from his knee after an infection. In Jul. 2026, Strowman wrestled his first match at GLCW The Return of the Titan. It marked his return since his last WWE SmackDown match in 2025. On the other hand, Redbeard was released from WWE in Apr. 2026, along with the other members of Wyatt Sicks. He has now competed across several independent promotions and events, including AWF, ACW, MLP Sacred Ground, TMW and ECPW Autumn Aggression. Redbeard is currently an active part of the Syx faction in TNA. They’re also 2-0 under new offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas since Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen earlier this month. Iowa’s defense ranks eighth in those same ratings, and the total is 40.5, so one sustained touchdown drive could decide this. Houston’s Conner Weigman and UCLA’s Ty Dieffenbach are both listed as questionable, and Clemson is handing former walk-on Trent Pearman a second straight start against South Carolina. Iowa has won 10 of the last 11 meetings and is on a four-game winning streak, with an outside shot at the playoff still alive. “There’s no one that runs the ball and stops the run better ,” Nebraska coach Matt Rhule said of Iowa this week. The Hawkeyes allow just 3.51 yards per rush, so the Huskers will need to move the ball through the air. Nebraska has the better offense for that. The Huskers rank 24th in ESPN’s offensive efficiency ratings, while Iowa ranks 45th, and they have a 47% passing success rate against FBS opponents. They’re also 2-0 under new offensive coordinator Glenn Thomas since Rhule fired Dana Holgorsen earlier this month. Iowa’s defense ranks eighth in those same ratings, and the total is 40.5, so one sustained touchdown drive could decide this. I trust Nebraska’s passing game to put that drive together and take the Heroes Trophy back to Lincoln. Picks: Nebraska 20-17, Nebraska +3.5, Under 40.5 Air Force (+6.5) at New Mexico: Upset watch 7 Air Force Falcons quarterback Evan Medders (5) runs with the ball in the second quarter against the UTEP Miners | Isaiah J. Downing-Imagn Images Kickoff: Friday, Nov. 27, 4:30 p.m. ET (The CW) Two 9-2 teams meet in Albuquerque with a Mountain West title game spot on the line. A New Mexico win guarantees the Lobos host the championship game and knocks Air Force out of contention. A Falcons win keeps their title hopes alive. Air Force leads the nation at 351.7 rushing yards per game, and New Mexico allows just 73.5. The Lobos won last year’s meeting 20-3 and held the Falcons to 110 rushing yards. This year’s Air Force offense still averages 5.66 yards per carry and runs successfully on 53.4% of its carries against FBS opponents. The bigger question is whether New Mexico can score enough. Quarterback Luke Moga is making only his second start of the season, and running backs Scottre Humphrey and Kiefer Sibley are questionable with ankle injuries . Humphrey leads the team in rushing. Air Force is also shorthanded on defense, with inside linebacker Blake Fletcher out for a second straight game. Air Force can win by putting together a pair of long touchdown drives and making Moga answer late. I like the Falcons to steal a one-point win and keep their title hopes going. Picks: Air Force 21-20, Air Force +6.5, Under 42.5 MORE: Week 13 college fantasy football rankings: Devon Dampier, Dylan Riley lead rivalry week South Carolina at Clemson (+6.5): Upset watch 6 Clemson quarterback Trent Pearman (14), one of the Tigers’ football seniors, poses with Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney before kickoff with Georgia Tech | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 3 p.m. ET (ESPN2) Clemson is 7-4 after Trent Pearman won his first career start, 20-10 at Duke. He completed 17 of 27 passes for 164 yards with no interceptions and ran for a touchdown while rotating with Chris Denson , who also scored on the ground. Pearman gets the start again because Christopher Vizzina is still out with a concussion. “He is nowhere near being back ,” coach Dabo Swinney said Sunday. “I don’t think people realize just how severe that was.” Clemson’s defense makes Pearman’s job manageable. The Tigers allow only 5.65 yards per dropback and held Duke to 10 points, so South Carolina will probably have to win on the ground. The Gamecocks average 5.42 yards per rush, Clemson allows 5.05, and quarterback LaNorris Sellers gives South Carolina a second runner the Tigers have to account for. If Clemson can keep the score in the teens heading into the fourth quarter, Pearman gets a chance to win it at home on the final possession. I still give South Carolina the late field goal, but 6.5 points is too many in a game this physical. Picks: South Carolina 20-17, Clemson +6.5, Under 42.5 No. 15 USC at No. 9 UCLA (+6.5): Upset watch 7.5 UCLA Bruins defensive back Scooter Jackson (1) celebrates in the end zone after returning an interception 65-yards for a touchdown in the second half against the Maryland Terrapins | Jamie Sabau-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 3:30 p.m. ET (CBS) A win clinches UCLA a spot in the Big Ten championship game, but the 10-1 Bruins are coming off an 18-16 triple-overtime loss at Michigan. Quarterback Ty Dieffenbach was carted off in the first overtime with a hip injury and is listed as questionable. Coach Bob Chesney said Dieffenbach is “ nowhere near in the clear ,” and Madden Iamaleava would make his first career start if Dieffenbach can’t go. UCLA’s defense is why I’m sticking with the upset I picked in this week’s prediction market column. The Bruins allow 4.22 yards per play and 4.89 yards per dropback. They rank fifth in ESPN’s defensive efficiency ratings, and USC’s offense ranks seventh. USC’s defense is the weaker unit at 69th, and it’s thin at the back. The Trojans ruled out safeties Kendarious Reddick, Trestin Castro and Isaiah Rubin , along with linebackers Taylor Johnson and Roman Marchetti. That sets up well for a Bruins running game averaging 5.75 yards per rush, whoever plays quarterback. UCLA can lean on the run at the Rose Bowl and make USC drive the length of the field. I have the Bruins winning by a field goal and clinching their trip to Indianapolis. Picks: UCLA 24-21, UCLA +6.5, Under 46.5 MORE: Week 13 CFB DFS picks: Cole Tabb, Nate Sheppard headline DraftKings, FanDuel value Kansas (+6) at Oklahoma State: Upset watch 5.5 Jayhawks running back Dylan Edwards (1) runs the ball during the first quarter against the West Virginia Mountaineers | Ben Queen-Imagn Images Kickoff: Saturday, Nov. 28, 6:15 p.m. ET (ESPN2) Kansas is 4-7 and out of the bowl picture after a 31-29 triple-overtime loss to BYU, but coach Lance Leipold isn’t expecting a flat finish in Stillwater. “We’ve got another game. There’s no quit . We’ll keep fighting,” Leipold said after the loss. Oklahoma State is 7-4 after an overtime comeback win at Arizona State. Kansas’s biggest worry is Oklahoma State’s passing game. Oklahoma State averages 8.09 yards per dropback, and Leipold had plenty of praise for quarterback Drew Mestemaker this week. “He’s really composed. He’s very accurate, strong arm, has all the measurables that you want at the next level,” Leipold said. Kansas allows just 6.08 yards per dropback. Holding Oklahoma State close to that number would take away the Cowboys’ fastest route to a double-digit lead. The Jayhawks also average 5.39 yards per rush, which gives them a way to shorten the game. Oklahoma State has the better offense overall, ranking 12th in ESPN’s offensive efficiency ratings, and its 5.53 yards per carry keeps defenses honest. I like the Cowboys in a shootout, but Kansas has enough on both sides of the ball to stay within six. item.title: Ross County have 102 goals and British football’s best start but is it a fairytale?
item.description: There is cynicism and jealousy but one of County’s top scorers is 39 as club try to climb leagues again after tumbling It was a vidiprinter moment worthy of a double take. Ross County 1 Cove Rangers 1 (Keir 52). Would Cove, scrapping for survival in Scottish League One, put an unlikely end last Saturday to the most emphatic run in British senior football? Don’t be silly, retorted County; four goals in the closing 17 minutes extended the Dingwall side’s goal difference to plus 45 (for 56, against 11). Played 16, won 14, drawn two. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. Taking in cup competitions they have scored 102 goals this season. Assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. We lost a dubious goal, which shouldn’t have stood.” Earlier in that competition County whacked 14 past a Hearts youth side before defeating a Celtic B team including two Chelsea loanees and a £3m midfielder. Continue reading...

item.title: Can Borussia Dortmund finally end their title wait? Three big questions for Bundesliga leaders
item.description: Niko Kovac’s team lead the way and, with Bayern Munich wounded, have a golden chance to be German champions for the first time in 15 years Borussia Dortmund’s dreams have a habit of becoming nightmares, like when they somehow handed Bayern Munich the Bundesliga title on the final day of the 2022-23 season. Or when an 89th-minute Arjen Robben goal won the 2013 Champions League final for the same opponents. Whenever Dortmund suffer heartbreak, it usually involves Bayern. As things stand, however, Niko Kovac’s side hold a two-point lead over Bayern at the top of the Bundesliga. Both teams are unbeaten, but Dortmund may be the more stable of the two at the moment, especially with Harry Kane expected to miss several months through injury. Continue reading...

item.title: Liam Delap’s struggles are symbolic of damaging Chelsea churn
item.description: The constant turnover of players and staff has made consistency an elusive quality at Stamford Bridge Liam Delap came and went. He joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 and was hailed by Enzo Maresca as the next Harry Kane. Fast forward a year, though, and there was no chance of Delap joining Kane in England’s World Cup squad. The striker’s form was miserable and the only surprise was that Chelsea made a profit when they sold him to Nottingham Forest for £50m last summer. On one level it looks like good business. Delap’s only season at Stamford Bridge featured one serious hamstring injury, one league goal, one ridiculous red card and not much else. Analysts at other clubs rated him at Ipswich and felt Chelsea was the wrong fit for his direct style of play. The mistake was less the decision not to give Delap another season, no matter the worries over cover for João Pedro, more the call to sign him in the first place. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. Simon Burnton Continue reading...

item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: Éric Cantona: ‘If I regret something about the kung fu kick, it’s that I would love to kick him in another place’
item.description: Before the release of a new documentary, the unrepentant Manchester United icon reflects on his deep bond with English football and his darker instincts “I’m an angel and a demon,” Éric Cantona says intently during a gripping new documentary about his life on and off the football pitch. “And an angel or a demon, you love him or you hate him. I’m far from being the person with the greatest integrity. I’m far from being the person who always tells the truth. I’m far from being the person who has never been hypocritical. Maybe I’m a good person, but I can also be a flower of evil. It’s the first time in my life I’ve realised this. I am a flower of evil, and I find it very beautiful.” It’s hard to know what to expect from the only written interview pinned to the release of Cantona: Flower of Evil . Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. Continue reading...

Joel Cantona has warned that his famous brother will walk out at any mention of the enduring crisis surrounding Manchester United , whether it’s a question about Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival or the Glazer family’s ruinous ownership of the club. item.title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We are on the edge’: how Swedish league declined from summit of women’s game
item.description: The Damallsvenskan once mastered Europe and attracted the best players, but many are now worried for its future On 12 October 2003, Sweden stood still. The women’s football team were playing Germany in the World Cup final. TV4 set a new viewing record as almost half the nation watched the game go into extra time, where Nia Künzer scored the golden goal winner after 98 minutes. It was a bitter pill to swallow but there was still the belief that the tournament would mark the start of women’s football’s commercial breakthrough in Sweden. After all, how could sponsors and broadcasters ignore such undeniable interest? Continue reading...

item.title: Neville, Carragher and the inescapable podcasting feedback loop of doom | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Even the best managers can struggle to escape ex-players’ need to manufacture a crisis for content. Enter Michael Carrick … A podcast studio in Manchester. A production runner pours water into jugs. Gary Neville enters the room with Michael Carrick. Neville: Just so you know, we’re already filming. This is the intro bit, where we show everyone coming on to set and doing some light banter. It humanises us. The viewer sees it and thinks we’re just mates chatting about football, rather than scions of a global podcast empire commercially obliged to produce an endless scroll of provocative content for money. I always say: why can’t you be both? Continue reading...

item.title: No drums, no tifo … no point? The impact of Palace’s missing Holmesdale Fanatics
item.description: Crystal Palace’s influential supporters’ group disbanded 24 hours before their first home game this season – and Selhurst Park has not been the same since Simon Teesdale could not help feeling mixed emotions when his beloved Crystal Palace won the Conference League in Leipzig in May. He started going to Selhurst Park with his father in the 1980s, became a season-ticket holder in the 1990s and has watched with pride as the club established itself as a permanent fixture in the Premier League over the past 14 years. Palace finally secured a major trophy in the 2025 FA Cup final – an experience Teesdale remembers as “one of the best days of my life” – and followed that up by winning the Conference League but he decided in August not to renew his season ticket. “Something happened between the FA Cup win and today that changed me,” he wrote in an emotional article published last month on his website. “Tipped me over the edge. Actually, it’s fairer to say that something accelerated in that period of time. The seeds were sown years ago.” Continue reading...

item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Manchester City get that empty feeling as they fail to win again
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Early in the second half of Tuesday night’s National League South match between Torquay United and Chesham, play was briefly suspended due to an ear-splitting din emitted over the Plainmoor public address system. “The game has stopped because the Torquay Tannoy system is making a loud noise that won’t stop,” posted Chesham on their Social Media Disgrace account. “I’m not kidding.” A sort of aural cross between an ocean liner’s foghorn and a party conference speech delivered by a senior member of the Reform party, it eventually stopped and play resumed with Torquay running out 2-1 winners. In this constantly changing world of global disruptions, uncertainties and risks, with social, political and economic disaffection seemingly on the rise everywhere, it’s genuinely heartening to know that some things never change . ‘Plus ça change, plus c’est la même chose’, as the late, great French writer Jean-Baptiste Alphonse Karr famously said, something that I’m sure Big Dunc is well aware of” – Noble Francis. May I be the 1,092nd correspondent to demand a review of the Letter o’ the Day award for Monday – and it be awarded to Declan Hackett for his letter foretelling the rescinding of the red card given to Lenny Yoro on Sunday? Given the precedent of awarding/revoking/re-awarding of the Afcon 2025 edition this would be entirely justified” – Peter Martin. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: Senegal regaining Afcon title is the right end to fiasco but issues do not stop there | Osasu Obayiuwana
item.description: After African football was dragged into needless disrepute the next step is to tackle two key areas of governance A journey of 310 days and three legal proceedings to confirm two things we know – that Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 to win the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations and, most importantly, that the decision of a referee remains final and sacrosanct – has produced the longest, most comical and embarrassing Afcon final in the tournament’s 69-year history. As the Confederation of African Football (Caf) executive committee member Samir Sobha told the Guardian, the decision of the organisation’s appeals board in March to overturn Senegal’s victory and award the title to Morocco, prompting a legal charade ended by the court of arbitration for sport’s verdict on Tuesday , was a “big joke” that brought Caf and the Afcon into needless disrepute. Continue reading...

item.title: Will Hajime Moriyasu get a high-profile job in Europe after his eight years in charge of Japan?
item.description: The coach will leave early after the postponement of the Asian Cup and, while there has been clear progress, some had hoped for better results at World Cups A popular Christmas tradition in Japan is to head to KFC but there is an unexpected item on the menu to chew over this year for the millions who do so – a meaty debate over Hajime Moriyasu’s eight years as national-team head coach. Among the many consequences of the Asian Cup’s postponement from January 2027 to December is the fact his tenure has ended early. The 58-year-old was supposed to stay on until February to cap that lengthy spell with (hopefully) a deserved trophy, hand over to Go Oiwa and then, perhaps, blaze a trail to Europe. Instead he left this month, after 113 games in charge during which Japan became a global force to be reckoned with, even if there are those who think he underdelivered. Continue reading...

item.title: The story of how Pelé and Maradona went from friends to bitter rivals
item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentinos Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | The game’s gone: has fantasy football been ruined by AI gafferbots?
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Sometimes, the beautiful game can make Football Daily feel old. Even Monday’s ostensibly old-school fixture between Brentford and Everton felt like the future destroying the past. The analytics-coded hosts prevailed 4-0 and James Tarkowski was dismissed by the VAR overlords for a challenge that would have been considered “firm but fair” on the muddy pitches of our youth. “I don’t think you can tackle like that in this day and age,” a misty-eyed David Moyes sighed after the game, before heading to the team bus to rewatch the Battle of Santiago . If Sunday was Gary Neville’s Sistine Chapel [ Monday’s Football Daily ], then his commentary on the Fernando Torres goal for Chelsea against Barcelona must be his David ” – Ronnie McMahon. Regarding Declan Hackett’s assertion [ Monday’s letters ] that Donald Trump will be helping his mate Mauricio Pochettino by ringing the FA to overturn Lenny Yoro’s red card, perhaps Poch should be careful what he wishes for: Trump may equally decide to get Michael Carrick reinstated, as he also has a bit of previous for that sort of thing” – Dexter O Riordan. In all the time that I have been watching football, I don’t think I have ever seen a player dismiss himself and be away down the tunnel before given a red card. Thanks James Tarkowski ” – Nigel Sanders. Brighton had only failed to win twice in the league since 5 September. A 1-1 draw with Leeds and a 2-0 defeat at Liverpool - their only opponents with double letters in their name. That bizarre hoodoo struck again at Hull on Sunday. Good good news for Seagulls fans is the only double-lettered encounters they have before hosting Hull in February are trips to Forest and Spurs. Even better news is that since that 1-1 draw with Leeds on 5 September, they have a 100% win record against sides without double letters and have not conceded a goal” – Dan Ashley (and no others). Continue reading...
